> Warning The C API v2 is not yet stable. Its interface may change in upcoming releases. See the [C API v2 overview]({% link docs/2.0/clients/c/v2/overview.md %}) for how to opt in and how to read the parameter ownership tags.

## API Reference Overview

<!-- This section is generated by scripts/generate_c_api_docs.py -->

### Common

#### `duckdb_v2_environment_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to the V2 environment: the required root through
which instance handles are created. All instances under one environment
share an instance cache, so file-level conflicts — the same database
file opened twice — are detected across them. Destroying the
environment refuses with ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE while any instance
created through it is still alive; destroy those first.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a DuckDB database instance: a buffer pool, a
scheduler, a set of GLOBAL settings, and the databases attached to it.
Created empty by [`duckdb_v2_instance_create`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create); databases are attached with
[`duckdb_v2_instance_attach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_attach), made the default with [`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default), and detached with
[`duckdb_v2_instance_detach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_detach). Always destroy via [`duckdb_v2_instance_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_instance_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a DuckDB connection: a session on a database
instance with its own LOCAL settings and transaction state. Always
destroy via [`duckdb_v2_connection_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_connection_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_handle`

A borrowed handle to the scope config options are read from and written
at. Taken from an instance ([`duckdb_v2_instance_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_instance_get_config)), a connection
([`duckdb_v2_connection_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_config)) or a context ([`duckdb_v2_context_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_config)),
and valid for as long as its source is; the caller never destroys it.
An instance's config is the GLOBAL scope alone; a connection's or a context's config reads that client's cascade
(its SESSION value, else the GLOBAL one, else the default) and writes at
any scope the option supports.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_option_handle`

An opaque, owned, read-only descriptor of a single config option as
registered on an instance: its canonical name, default value,
description, the scopes it may be written at, and aliases. It carries no
current value: read that with the *_get_option_value functions, and
write it with the *_set_option functions. Returned by the
*_get_option_by_name and *_get_option_by_index functions; the caller
always destroys it via [`duckdb_v2_option_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_option_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_handle`

Opaque detail for a failed call; destroy with [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a logical type. Carries a type id plus any
kind-specific metadata: decimal width and scale, enum dictionary, list /
array / struct / map / union child types, alias. A type is read-only once
constructed; instances arrive from a query result schema, or from one of
the create_type_* constructors. Always destroy via [`duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy).
Borrowed strings returned by the getters are valid only until then.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_value_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a single SQL value: a logical type plus a
typed payload. Always destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). The string returned by
[`duckdb_v2_value_get_varchar`](#duckdb_v2_value_get_varchar) / [`duckdb_v2_value_get_blob`](#duckdb_v2_value_get_blob) is borrowed and valid only until then.
That holds for BIGNUM too, where what is borrowed is the opaque storage
form; [`duckdb_v2_bignum_decode`](#duckdb_v2_bignum_decode) translates it into a magnitude and a sign flag,
writing into a buffer the caller supplies.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_result_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to the streaming result of a query. Carries the
schema (column names and logical types), the statement type, and the
result type from prepare time; row data is produced incrementally by
stepping ([`duckdb_v2_result_step`](#duckdb_v2_result_step)) or draining ([`duckdb_v2_result_fetch_chunk`](#duckdb_v2_result_fetch_chunk)). Single consumer:
step from one thread at a time.

A result is a cursor on the connection's execution, not a box of data.
While its statement runs — at most until it is finished, cancelled,
errored, or destroyed — the connection refuses new queries with
ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE, and the query's transaction stays open, deferring
version cleanup and checkpointing, so drain or destroy it promptly. Side-effecting statements
(PRAGMA, ALTER, ...) take effect only once the result is drained. Always
destroy via [`duckdb_v2_result_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_result_destroy), which is safe even on a partially consumed
stream.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a data chunk: a set of vectors of equal
logical length plus a cardinality (row count).

A data chunk is the main “unit of execution” in DuckDB, and the main unit of data transfer in the API.
It may be owned or borrowed, depending on the context.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_vector_handle`

A borrowed handle to a vector within a data chunk, carrying a part of a column's values.
Vectors are always borrowed from a data chunk, and are valid only as long as their parent data chunk is alive.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_arena_handle`

A borrowed handle to a “arena allocator”. 

Bytes handed out by [`duckdb_v2_arena_allocate`](#duckdb_v2_arena_allocate) share the same lifetime as the arena itself.
[`duckdb_v2_vector_get_arena`](#duckdb_v2_vector_get_arena) yields the arena backing the out-of-line bytes of non-inlined VARCHAR / BLOB / BIT / BIGNUM 
values, valid until the owning vector is flattened, reallocated, or destroyed.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_context_handle`

A borrowed handle to a client context: a connection seen from inside
DuckDB. Handed out within DuckDB-managed scopes — function bind / init /
exec callbacks, replacement scans, and the extension entrypoint — and
valid only for the duration of that scope; the caller never destroys it.
Within that scope a transaction is already active. A context reaches
the same capabilities a connection does, through
[`duckdb_v2_context_get_factory`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_factory), [`duckdb_v2_context_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_config),
[`duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system) and [`duckdb_v2_context_log`](#duckdb_v2_context_log).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_handle`

A borrowed handle to the scope values, types, data chunks and column
data collections are created in. Taken from an instance
([`duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory`](#duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory)), a connection
([`duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory)) or a context ([`duckdb_v2_context_get_factory`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_factory)),
and valid for as long as its source is; the caller never destroys it.
A factory resolves in the scope of its source: a connection's or a
context's factory reaches the catalog and the client's settings, while an
instance's factory knows only the built-in types and casts, with
default settings, and refuses anything that needs a catalog.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_text_sink_fn`

Receives text produced by DuckDB

Invoked exactly once per producing call, with the complete text in a
single view.

The view is borrowed for the duration of the call only. Copy what you
need before returning, and do not retain `text` or `text->ptr`. The bytes are NOT guaranteed to be null-terminated.

`err` is a live error slot, never NULL. Populate it with
[`duckdb_v2_error_info_set_code`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_set_code) / [`duckdb_v2_error_info_set_text`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_set_text) to signal failure to DuckDB. Do not destroy it yourself.

The sink runs inside DuckDB's call frame: it must not throw or unwind across the boundary, and it must not 
re-enter the API on the handle being operated on.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_text_sink_fn)(
  const duckdb_v2_str *text,
  void *user_data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `text`: Borrowed view of the complete text. Valid only until the sink returns.
* `user_data`: The opaque pointer handed to the producing call alongside the callback, passed through untouched.
* `err`: Live error slot, never NULL. Populate it to fail the producing call; do not destroy it. (out)

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_opaque_equals_fn`

Compares two caller-defined resources for equality.

Invoked when DuckDB needs to compare two opaque handles. The callback is
responsible for interpreting the pointers and comparing the underlying
resources. Return true if they are equal, false otherwise.

The callback runs inside DuckDB's call frame: it must not throw or unwind across the boundary, and it must not 
re-enter the API on the handle being operated on.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef bool (*duckdb_v2_opaque_equals_fn)(
  void *a,
  void *b
);
```

##### Parameters

* `a`: Opaque pointer to the first resource to compare.
* `b`: Opaque pointer to the second resource to compare.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_opaque_destroy_fn`

Destroys a caller-defined resource.

Invoked when DuckDB needs to destroy an opaque handle. The callback is
responsible for interpreting the pointer and freeing the underlying
resource.

The callback runs inside DuckDB's call frame: it must not throw or unwind across the boundary, and it must not 
re-enter the API on the handle being operated on.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_opaque_destroy_fn)(
  void *data
);
```

##### Parameters

* `data`: Opaque pointer to the resource to destroy. The callback is responsible for freeing it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sel_t`

An entry in a selection-vector.

A selection-vector is a “dictionary” represented as an array of indices (sel_t's) mapping “logical” row indices to 
the “physical” offsets in a vectors primary data buffer. Used by “dictionary vectors” to represent a filtered or 
“sparse” view of the vector's data.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef uint32_t duckdb_v2_sel_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_varchar_t`

VARCHAR storage. The bytes must contain valid UTF-8.
Read the transparent bytes fields directly.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef duckdb_v2_bytes duckdb_v2_varchar_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_blob_t`

BLOB storage. Read the transparent bytes fields directly.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef duckdb_v2_bytes duckdb_v2_blob_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_bit_t`

BIT storage. Byte 0 is the padding-bit count, bytes 1.. the data.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef duckdb_v2_bytes duckdb_v2_bit_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_bignum_t`

BIGNUM storage. Decode via [`duckdb_v2_bignum_decode`](#duckdb_v2_bignum_decode).

##### Syntax

```c
typedef duckdb_v2_bytes duckdb_v2_bignum_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_identifier_t`

A borrowed name view with the same layout as str, marking a string
DuckDB treats as a SQL identifier: one matched case-insensitively.
Compare two identifiers case-insensitively rather than byte for byte, and
render one into SQL through the identifier-quoting entry point rather
than embedding it raw. The catalog preserves casing; some registries
(config settings) canonicalize to lowercase.

An identifier passed into the API must be valid UTF-8; otherwise the
call fails with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef duckdb_v2_str duckdb_v2_identifier_t;
```

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_str`

A borrowed, length-delimited string view: `ptr` points at `len` bytes of
character data. The bytes are NOT guaranteed to be null-terminated and
may contain interior null bytes, so always honor `len` rather than
scanning for a terminator. The view never owns its bytes; the function
that produced it documents how long they live (typically "valid until the
owning handle is destroyed"). `{NULL, 0}` is the canonical empty view,
and `ptr` must not be dereferenced when `len` is 0. Not to be confused
with `bytes`, the transparent 16-byte *storage* format for a
variable-size value in a vector.

Functions take an input view as a `const str *`, which must not be
NULL; a NULL pointer, or a view whose `ptr` is NULL while `len` is
nonzero, fails with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. Point at a `{NULL, 0}` view to
pass an empty string.

Text inputs, such as VARCHAR values and names, must contain valid UTF-8.
The caller is responsible for ensuring this; API functions do not
necessarily validate the input.
Binary inputs, such as BLOB values, do not require valid UTF-8.

##### Fields

* `ptr` (`const char *`)
* `len` (`idx_t`)

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_bytes`

16-byte storage for a variable-size, byte-backed value: VARCHAR, BLOB,
BIT, or BIGNUM. The bytes are inlined when the length is at most
BYTES_INLINE_LENGTH, in value.inlined.inlined; otherwise
value.pointer.ptr holds them and value.pointer.prefix repeats the first
4. The union is transparent, so read the fields directly. VARCHAR and
BLOB carry no further encoding; BIT and BIGNUM do. For BIT, byte 0 is the
padding-bit count and bytes 1.. are the data; BIGNUM is decoded via
[`duckdb_v2_bignum_decode`](#duckdb_v2_bignum_decode).

##### Fields

* `value` (`union`)
    * `pointer` (`struct`)
        * `length` (`uint32_t`)
        * `prefix` (`char[4]`)
        * `ptr` (`char *`)
    * `inlined` (`struct`)
        * `length` (`uint32_t`)
        * `inlined` (`char[12]`)

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_opaque`

An opaque, owned handle to a caller-defined resource. Bundles the pointer
with optional callbacks that destroy and compare the resource.

##### Fields

* `ptr` (`void *`)
* `destroy` (`duckdb_v2_opaque_destroy_fn`)
* `equals` (`duckdb_v2_opaque_equals_fn`)

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_ORDER_PRESERVATION`

The order guarantee a producer of rows makes about its output, which decides whether the rows it produces
must be kept in order downstream.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_ORDER_PRESERVATION_NO_ORDER` = 0: The rows have no meaningful order. The engine may reorder them freely, and consumers that otherwise keep
insertion order, such as query results, INSERT and COPY, run in parallel without ordering them.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ORDER_PRESERVATION_INSERTION_ORDER` = 1: The rows are produced in insertion order, which the engine keeps unless the `preserve_insertion_order`
setting is disabled.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ORDER_PRESERVATION_FIXED_ORDER` = 2: The rows are produced in an order that must be kept, as if sorted by an `ORDER BY`, even when the
`preserve_insertion_order` setting is disabled.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_BYTES_INLINE_LENGTH`

Inline cutoff for `bytes` storage: a value of at most this many bytes is stored inline.

Value: `12`.

<br>

### Errors

#### `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

Error codes for API calls.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_NONE` = 0: Success.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_API` = 1: Generic API error.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_FILE_NOT_FOUND` = 1001: The specified file could not be found.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_READ_FAILURE` = 1002: Failed to read from the storage device.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_EOF` = 1003: Unexpected end of file reached.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_GENERAL` = 1004: A generic I/O error occurred while reading or writing data.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_NETWORK` = 1005: A network-level failure occurred during an I/O operation.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_IO_HTTP` = 1006: An HTTP request issued by the database failed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` = 2001: General invalid input error.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_PARAMETER_INVALID` = 2002: A specific function parameter is malformed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE` = 2003: A provided value is outside the acceptable range.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE` = 2004: An object exceeded its maximum permitted size.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_METADATA_DEFERRED` = 2005: The metadata asked for is known only once execution binds the statement that produces it, because the statement expands into several. Step the result and ask again.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE` = 3001: The requested resource is already in use.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_OUT_OF_MEMORY` = 3002: An allocation failed because the system ran out of memory.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_CONNECTION` = 3003: A connection-level failure occurred (e.g. the connection has been closed or invalidated).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_DEPENDENCY` = 3004: An operation failed because of an unresolved dependency between catalog objects.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_MISSING_EXTENSION` = 3005: An extension required by the operation is not loaded.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RESOURCE_AUTOLOAD` = 3006: Autoloading an extension failed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_CONVERSION` = 4001: A value could not be converted to the requested type.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_UNKNOWN` = 4002: An unknown or unsupported type was encountered.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_INVALID` = 4003: A type was used in a context where it is not valid.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_MISMATCH` = 4004: Two values or expressions have incompatible types.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_DECIMAL` = 4005: A decimal value is out of range or otherwise invalid.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_TYPE_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` = 4006: Division by zero was attempted.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_PARSER` = 5001: The query could not be parsed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_SYNTAX` = 5002: The query contains a syntax error.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_BINDER` = 5003: Binding the query against the catalog failed (e.g. unknown column or table).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_PLANNER` = 5004: The query could not be translated into a logical plan.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_OPTIMIZER` = 5005: An error occurred during query optimization.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_EXPRESSION` = 5006: An expression in the query is invalid or could not be evaluated.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_EXECUTOR` = 5007: An error occurred while executing the physical plan.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_SCHEDULER` = 5008: The task scheduler reported an error while running the query.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` = 5009: The requested feature or operation is not implemented.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_PARAMETER_NOT_RESOLVED` = 5010: A prepared-statement parameter has not been bound to a value.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_QUERY_PARAMETER_NOT_ALLOWED` = 5011: A prepared-statement parameter was used in a position where it is not allowed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_CATALOG` = 6001: A catalog operation failed (e.g. object not found or already exists).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_TRANSACTION` = 6002: A transaction-level error occurred (e.g. conflict or aborted transaction).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_CONSTRAINT` = 6003: A constraint (primary key, unique, foreign key, NOT NULL, check) was violated.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_INDEX` = 6004: An index operation failed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_SEQUENCE` = 6005: A sequence operation failed (e.g. overflow or invalid usage).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_STATISTICS` = 6006: An error related to catalog statistics occurred.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_DATABASE_SERIALIZATION` = 6007: Serializing or deserializing a database object failed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_CONFIGURATION_SETTINGS` = 7001: A settings-related error occurred (e.g. setting an unknown option).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_CONFIGURATION_INVALID` = 7002: The database configuration is invalid.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_CONFIGURATION_PERMISSION` = 7003: The operation is not permitted under the current configuration.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RUNTIME_INTERNAL` = 8001: An internal invariant was violated; this indicates a bug in DuckDB.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RUNTIME_FATAL` = 8002: A fatal error occurred; the database is no longer usable.
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RUNTIME_INTERRUPT` = 8003: The operation was interrupted (e.g. by a cancel request).
* `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_RUNTIME_NULL_POINTER` = 8004: A required pointer was unexpectedly null.

### Function Properties

#### `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_KEY`

Identifies a configurable function property. Pass one of these to
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_property`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_property) or [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_property`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_property) together with a
matching [`DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_VALUE`](#duckdb_v2_function_property_value). The high byte is the function-type
group: COMMON (`0x01xxxx`) keys apply to all function types, while
group-specific keys (e.g. aggregate `0x03xxxx`) are only valid for that
function type and are rejected with an error otherwise.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_STABILITY` = 65536: How stable/deterministic the function's result is across rows and queries. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_STABILITY_*` values. Defaults to `CONSISTENT`.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_NULL_HANDLING` = 65792: Whether the function handles NULL inputs itself. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_NULL_HANDLING_*` values. Defaults to `DEFAULT` (NULL in, NULL out).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_FALLIBILITY` = 66048: Whether the function can raise a runtime error. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_FALLIBILITY_*` values. Functions created through this API default to `FALLIBLE`, since their callbacks can report errors.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_COLLATION_HANDLING` = 66304: How the function interacts with collations on its arguments. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_COLLATION_HANDLING_*` values. Defaults to `PROPAGATE`.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_ORDER_DEPENDENT` = 196608: Aggregate only. Whether the aggregate's result depends on the order in which rows are aggregated. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_ORDER_DEPENDENT_*` values. Defaults to `YES`.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_DISTINCT_DEPENDENT` = 196864: Aggregate only. Whether the aggregate's result is affected by a DISTINCT modifier. Accepts the `FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_DISTINCT_DEPENDENT_*` values. Defaults to `YES`.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_VALUE`

A value for a [`DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_KEY`](#duckdb_v2_function_property_key). Each key owns a 256-value block: a
value `V` is valid for key `K` iff `(V & 0xFFFF00) == K`, and shares the
key's function-type group (`V & 0xFF0000`) in its high byte. Passing a
value that does not match the key is rejected with an error. Boolean-like
properties are expressed as named values so that additional values can be
added later without breaking the ABI.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_STABILITY_CONSISTENT` = 65536: The function always returns the same result given the same input.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_STABILITY_VOLATILE` = 65537: The result may differ per row (e.g. random()).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_STABILITY_CONSISTENT_WITHIN_QUERY` = 65538: The result is stable within a single query/transaction but may change across queries (e.g. now()).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_NULL_HANDLING_DEFAULT` = 65792: Default NULL handling: if any argument is NULL the result is NULL and the function is not invoked for that row.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_NULL_HANDLING_SPECIAL` = 65793: The function handles NULL inputs itself and is invoked even when arguments are NULL.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_FALLIBILITY_INFALLIBLE` = 66048: The function never raises a runtime error. Declaring this promises that the callbacks never report an error; an error reported anyway becomes an internal error.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_FALLIBILITY_FALLIBLE` = 66049: The function may raise a runtime error for some inputs.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_COLLATION_HANDLING_PROPAGATE` = 66304: The function combines collations from its inputs and propagates them to its result (default).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_COLLATION_HANDLING_PUSH_COMBINABLE` = 66305: Combinable collations are executed on the input arguments before the function runs.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_COLLATION_HANDLING_IGNORE` = 66306: Collations are ignored by the function.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_ORDER_DEPENDENT_YES` = 196608: The aggregate's result depends on the order in which rows are aggregated (default).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_ORDER_DEPENDENT_NO` = 196609: The aggregate's result does not depend on input order.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_DISTINCT_DEPENDENT_YES` = 196864: The aggregate's result is affected by a DISTINCT modifier (default).
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_AGG_DISTINCT_DEPENDENT_NO` = 196865: The aggregate's result is not affected by a DISTINCT modifier.

<br>

### Arena

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_arena_allocate"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_arena_allocate</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_arena_handle</span> <span class="nv">arena</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">byte_len</span>, <span class="kt">uint8_t</span> **<span class="nv">out_ptr</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_arena_allocate`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Allocate `byte_len` bytes from the arena.

Returns a writable pointer to `byte_len` uninitialized bytes, valid for as long as the arena is. There is no
minimum or maximum allocation size, and the arena may return a pointer to a block of memory that is larger than 
`byte_len`. The arena will free all allocated memory when it is destroyed, so the caller should not attempt to free the returned pointer themselves.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_arena_allocate(
  duckdb_v2_arena_handle arena,
  idx_t byte_len,
  uint8_t **out_ptr,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `arena`: The arena to allocate from.
* `byte_len`: Number of bytes to reserve. May be 0.
* `out_ptr`: Receives a writable pointer to byte_len arena-owned bytes. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Cast

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a cast function being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_create), configured with the setter functions (e.g.
[`duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type), [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback), etc.), made available with
[`duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a cast function during the execution “exec” phase.
The “exec” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the input vector, the output vector to
write into, the number of rows to convert, and the mode the cast is running in.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE`

The mode a cast is being executed in. A normal cast must either succeed
for every row or report an error, which aborts the query. A “try” cast
(SQL TRY_CAST, and implicit casts the engine probes speculatively)
tolerates per-row failures: the callback writes NULL for the rows it
could not convert instead of aborting. Read with
[`duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode), and passed to [`duckdb_v2_vector_cast`](#duckdb_v2_vector_cast).

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE_NORMAL` = 0: A regular cast. A conversion failure reported through the error slot aborts the query.
* `DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE_TRY` = 1: A “try” cast. Conversion failures should be written as NULLs into the output vector; an error reported through the slot is swallowed and the affected rows are left NULL.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> *<span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">source_type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_target_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_target_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">target_type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_implicit_cast_cost"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_implicit_cast_cost</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">int64_t</span> <span class="nv">cost</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_opaque</span> *<span class="nv">data</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_callback_fn</span> <span class="nv">callback</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">void</span> **<span class="nv">data</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_input"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_input</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_vector_handle</span> *<span class="nv">vector</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_output"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_output</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_vector_handle</span> *<span class="nv">vector</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE</span> *<span class="nv">mode</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_extension_handle</span> <span class="nv">extension</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle</span> *<span class="nv">function</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new cast function through a factory.

The function starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type),
[`duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback), etc.), then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function). The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy), also after registration.

The cast function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the cast function through.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created cast function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the type the cast converts from.

The type is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous source type. A source type must
be set before registration, and it must be a fully defined concrete type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_source_type(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle source_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the source type of.
* `source_type`: The type to cast from. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_target_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the type the cast converts to.

The type is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous target type. A target type must
be set before registration, and it must be a fully defined concrete type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_target_type(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle target_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the target type of.
* `target_type`: The type to cast to. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_implicit_cast_cost`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets what it costs to apply this cast implicitly.

The binder uses the cost to choose between candidate implicit casts: a lower non-negative cost makes the
cast more likely to be picked, a higher one less likely. Built-in widening casts sit in the [0, 20] range,
so a cost above 100 effectively puts this cast last. A negative cost -- the default -- means the cast is
never applied implicitly and is reached only through an explicit CAST or TRY_CAST.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_implicit_cast_cost(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  int64_t cost,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the implicit cast cost of.
* `cost`: The cost. Negative disables implicit casting.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the cast function.

Associates an opaque pointer with the function, retrievable from the exec callback via
[`duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data). The opaque handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor,
invoked when the data is no longer needed. The data is read-only during execution: the same pointer is
shared by every thread running the cast.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the exec callback of the cast function.

The exec callback implements the conversion: it is invoked during query execution with a batch of input
values and must fill the output vector. An exec callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_exec_callback(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the exec callback of.
* `callback`: The exec callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the user data set via [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_set_user_data).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `data`: Receives the user data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns how many rows this execution must convert.

The number of rows held by the input vector, and the number of entries the callback must write to the
output vector. Note that this may be less than a full vector: a constant input is converted as a single
row and the result is expanded by the engine.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `count`: Receives the number of rows. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_input`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the input vector holding the values to convert.

The vector holds the source type's values for the current batch; use [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count)
for the number of rows. Borrowed; valid only for the duration of the callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_input(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_vector_handle *vector,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `vector`: Receives the borrowed input vector. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_output`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the output vector the exec callback must write into.

The callback must write one entry per input row; use [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_row_count) for the number
of rows. Borrowed; valid only for the duration of the callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_output(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_vector_handle *vector,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `vector`: Receives the borrowed output vector to write into. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the mode the cast is being executed in.

In `CAST_MODE_TRY` a conversion failure should be written as a NULL into the output vector rather than
reported through the error slot, since the engine discards the error and keeps whatever the callback left
in the output.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_get_mode(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_exec_info_handle info,
  DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE *mode,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `mode`: Receives the cast mode. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the cast function, making it available to CAST and TRY_CAST.

The cast is registered on the connection's database and takes effect immediately for every connection; it is not
part of the connection's transaction, so a rollback does not undo it. Registration requires a source type, a
target type and an exec callback; both types must be fully defined concrete types. Registering a cast for a pair
that already has one replaces it. The cast function must have been created through a factory of the same database.
The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy), which
does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_cast_function(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `function`: The cast function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the cast function, making it available to CAST and TRY_CAST.

The cast is registered on the loading extension's database. Use this from the extension's load callback.
Registration requires a source type, a target type and an exec callback; both types must be fully defined concrete
types. Registering a cast for a pair that already has one replaces it. The cast function must have been created
through a factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it
with [`duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_cast_function(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `function`: The cast function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the cast function, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered
function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_cast_function_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_cast_function_handle *function
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Column Data Collection

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle`

A column data collection represents a set of (buffer-managed) data chunks.

You can append chunks to the collection iteratively, and then scan the collection back to retrieve the chunks in order. 
DuckDB will manage the memory for the chunks, and transparently offload chunks to disk if necessary.
A collection shall not be scanned while it is being appended to, and vice versa.
A collection shall not be appended to concurrently, but it can be scanned concurrently by multiple threads using a shared scan state and per-thread worker scan states. For concurrent appends, consider creating multiple collections and “combining” them into one collection at the end.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_shared_scan_state_handle`

Opaque state handle for shared state across multiple threads scanning a column data collection. This is used to coordinate work distribution, track global progress, or store any other state that needs to be shared across threads during the scan of the collection.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_handle`

Opaque state handle for local state while scanning a column data collection. This is used to track progress and any other state that needs to be maintained on a per-thread basis across calls while scanning the collection. It also keeps the buffers backing the most recently scanned chunk alive: chunks are scanned zero-copy, so a scanned chunk's data is only valid until the worker state's next scan call or its destruction.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append_state_handle`

Opaque state handle for appending to a column data collection. This is used to track progress and any other state that needs to be maintained across calls while appending to the collection.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates an empty column data collection from a factory.

Allocates a new, empty column data collection, drawing its buffers from the factory's database. The collection starts with no chunks and is ready to have chunks appended to it. A collection must have at least one column; an empty types array is rejected with INVALID_INPUT.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  const duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *types_array,
  idx_t types_count,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle *out_collection,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create with.
* `types_array`: Pointer to an array of logical_type handles, one per column. This defines the schema for the chunks that will be stored in the collection. All chunks appended to this collection must have vectors that conform to these types.
* `types_count`: Number of elements in the types_array.
* `out_collection`: Receives the new collection handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_reset`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Drops all buffered rows, keeping the column types.

Drops all buffered rows and releases their memory. The column types are
unchanged and the collection is immediately appendable again. Existing
append and scan states are invalidated. Use
[`duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_clear`](#duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_clear) instead to keep the memory for the
next appends.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_reset(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to reset.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_clear`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Drops all buffered rows, keeping the column types and the memory.

Like [`duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_reset`](#duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_reset), but the buffers are retained
rather than released, so the next appends write into memory that is
already allocated. Use this when the collection is refilled repeatedly.
The column types are unchanged and the collection is immediately
appendable again. Existing append and scan states are invalidated.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_clear(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to clear.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a column data collection and all its chunks.

Cleans up the collection and all resources associated with it, including all contained chunks. Sets the collection handle to NULL.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle *collection
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_combine`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Merges the source collection into the target collection, consuming the source in the process.

Transfers all chunks from the source collection to the target collection. This destroys the source collection, setting the source handle to NULL. The two collections must have the same column types, and must have been created from factories of the same database: the transferred chunks keep their original buffers, so combining collections from different databases would tie the target to a buffer manager it does not own.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_combine(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle target,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle *source,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `target`: The collection to merge into. After the call, this collection will contain all chunks from both collections.
* `source`: The collection to merge from. This collection will be destroyed by this operation and its handle set to NULL.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_row_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the total number of rows across all chunks in the collection.

Sums the row counts of all chunks in the collection. This is the total number of rows represented by the collection, which may be more than the number of rows in any individual chunk.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_row_count(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  idx_t *out_row_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to inspect.
* `out_row_count`: Receives the total row count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append_state_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Initializes an append state for the collection.

Returns an append state handle that can be used to append chunks to the collection while maintaining any necessary state across calls.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append_state_create(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,

```

##### Parameters

* `out_state`: Receives the new append state handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys an append state handle.

Cleans up any resources associated with the append state. After this call, the state handle must not be used again.

##### Syntax


`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Appends a data chunk to the collection.

Appends a copy of the given chunk to the end of the collection. The
chunk's column count and types must equal the collection's exactly; a
mismatch is rejected with INVALID_INPUT before anything is copied.
VARCHAR values must already contain valid UTF-8; this function does not validate text.
Complex-typed vectors may be flattened in place by the copy.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_append_state_handle state,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to append to.
* `state`: The append state to use this append operation.
* `chunk`: The chunk to append.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

Cleans up any resources associated with the shared scan state. After this call, the state handle must not be used again.

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Initializes a worker scan state for the collection.

Returns a “local” scan state handle for a worker thread to use while scanning the collection. This allows each thread to maintain its own progress and any other necessary information across multiple scan calls, while still coordinating with other threads via the shared scan state.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_create(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_handle *out_state,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to prepare for worker scanning.
* `out_state`: Receives the new worker scan state handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a worker scan state handle.

Cleans up any resources associated with the worker scan state. After this call, the state handle must not be used again.

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_destroy(

```

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_scan`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Scans the collection to retrieve the next data chunk, using shared state for coordination across threads and worker-local state for individual progress tracking.

Retrieves the next chunk of data from the collection based on the provided shared scan state and worker-local scan state. The output chunk's column count and types must equal the collection's exactly; a mismatch is rejected with INVALID_INPUT.

The scan is zero-copy where possible: the output chunk's vectors may reference the collection's buffers, kept alive by the worker scan state. The chunk's data is therefore only valid until the next scan call with the same worker state, or until the worker state or the collection is destroyed, whichever comes first. Copy the data out (or append it to another collection) before continuing the scan if it must outlive that window.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_scan(
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_shared_scan_state_handle shared_state,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_worker_scan_state_handle worker_state,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle out_chunk,
  bool *did_produce_chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `collection`: The collection to scan.
* `shared_state`: The shared scan state to use for coordinating across threads.
* `worker_state`: The worker-local scan state to use for this thread's scan operation.
* `out_chunk`: The output chunk to write to.
* `did_produce_chunk`: Receives true when a chunk was produced by this call, or false when the scan has completed (the chunk is then reset to empty). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Configuration

#### `DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE`

The scope of an option's value. Writes take DEFAULT, GLOBAL or SESSION:
DEFAULT writes to the option's default scope ([`duckdb_v2_option_get_default_scope`](#duckdb_v2_option_get_default_scope)),
like SQL `SET name = value`; GLOBAL writes through to the instance, visible to all
connections, like `SET GLOBAL`; SESSION writes to one connection's session
only, like `SET SESSION`. Reads report GLOBAL or SESSION, as DuckDB
attributes the value: an option no scope sets reads as GLOBAL, its
default, and a legacy option read through a connection or context reads
as SESSION.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE_DEFAULT` = 0: Write only: the option's default scope ([`duckdb_v2_option_get_default_scope`](#duckdb_v2_option_get_default_scope)), not its default value.
* `DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE_GLOBAL` = 1: The instance's value, visible to all connections.
* `DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE_SESSION` = 2: A connection's session value.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_get_config`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the config of an instance: the GLOBAL scope.

Reads report GLOBAL, and writes are `SET GLOBAL`. Writing at SESSION
scope returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID: an instance has no session. Options
that can only be chosen at startup are passed to [`duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options).
The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid for as long as the instance
is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_get_config(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_config_handle *out_config,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance.
* `out_config`: Receives the borrowed config. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_get_config`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the config of a connection.

Reads follow the connection's cascade: its SESSION value if it set one,
otherwise the GLOBAL value, otherwise the default. Writes accept any
scope the option supports. The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid
for as long as the connection is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_get_config(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_config_handle *out_config,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection.
* `out_config`: Receives the borrowed config. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_context_get_config`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the config of a context.

The same scope [`duckdb_v2_connection_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_config) gives for the context's
connection. The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid for as long as
the context is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_context_get_config(
  duckdb_v2_context_handle ctx,
  duckdb_v2_config_handle *out_config,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `ctx`: The context.
* `out_config`: Receives the borrowed config. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_get_option_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reads the effective value of an option in this config, and the scope it
came from.

Aliases resolve transparently, and an unknown name returns
ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. The caller destroys the returned value.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_get_option_value(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *out_value,
  DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE *out_scope,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config to read from.
* `name`: Option name (canonical or alias).
* `out_value`: Receives the value, typed as the option. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `out_scope`: Receives the scope the value came from. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes an option in this config.

`scope` chooses the destination, mirroring SQL:
  * DEFAULT writes to the option's default scope, like a bare
    `SET name = value`.
  * GLOBAL writes through to the instance, visible to all connections,
    like `SET GLOBAL`.
  * SESSION writes to one connection's session only, like `SET SESSION`.
A scope neither the option ([`duckdb_v2_option_supports_scope`](#duckdb_v2_option_supports_scope)) nor the config
supports returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID; an instance's config supports only
GLOBAL. The value is cast to the option's type as SQL `SET` does. An
unknown name is rejected unless an extension that defines it can be
autoloaded. An option that can only be chosen at startup is rejected:
pass it to [`duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE scope,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config to write to.
* `name`: Option name (canonical or alias).
* `value`: The value, cast to the option's type as SQL `SET` does. Borrowed.
* `scope`: Target scope: DEFAULT, GLOBAL, or SESSION.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_set_option_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes an option in this config from text, the form SQL `SET` accepts.

[`duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value`](#duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value) with the text as a VARCHAR value: the engine casts
it to the option's type, so this is the one-call form for a setting
spelled the way SQL spells it, e.g. “1GB” for memory_limit. Scope
handling and errors are [`duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value`](#duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value)'s.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_set_option_text(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  const duckdb_v2_str *setting,
  DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE scope,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config to write to.
* `name`: Option name (canonical or alias).
* `setting`: The setting, in the textual form SQL `SET` accepts.
* `scope`: Target scope: DEFAULT, GLOBAL, or SESSION.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_get_option_by_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Describes a config option registered on this config's instance, by name.

Allocates an option descriptor: canonical name, default value,
description, supported and default scopes, and aliases. Aliases resolve transparently — passing an alias returns the
canonical option, with the alias listed in its alias array. An unknown
name returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID, which includes an option of an
extension that has not loaded yet. The caller destroys the returned
option.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_get_option_by_name(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_option_handle *out_option,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config whose instance registered the options.
* `name`: Option name (canonical or alias).
* `out_option`: Receives the option descriptor. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_get_option_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of config options registered on this config's instance.

Counts core options plus the extension options registered on this
instance. Aliases are NOT counted separately; each one is reachable
through its canonical option's alias array.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_get_option_count(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config whose instance registered the options.
* `out_count`: Receives the option count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_config_get_option_by_index`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Describes the config option at the given index on this config's instance.

Index space: [0, core_count) addresses core options, [core_count, total)
extension options. The mapping is stable for as long as no extension
registers new options. An out-of-range index returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.
The caller destroys the returned option.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_config_get_option_by_index(
  duckdb_v2_config_handle config,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_option_handle *out_option,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `config`: The config whose instance registered the options.
* `index`: The option index, in [0, option_count).
* `out_option`: Receives the option descriptor. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_option_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys an option descriptor.

Frees the handle along with the strings it owns. On success the slot is
set to null. Safe to call on an already-null slot.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_option_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_option_handle *option
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option handle to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_option_supports_scope`

```c
);
```

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`
