#### `duckdb_v2_connection_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Opens a connection to an instance.

Each connection carries its own client context and session-scoped (LOCAL)
settings. Connections to the same instance share its catalog, buffer
pool, and transaction manager. A connection may be created before any
database is attached to the instance; until one is, only the system
catalog and the connection's temporary catalog are visible. The caller
destroys it via [`duckdb_v2_connection_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_connection_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_create(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle *out_conn,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance to connect to.
* `out_conn`: Receives the new connection handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the connection.

Always succeeds. Releases the connection's reference on the underlying
database instance, which survives for as long as anything else still
references it. On success the handle is set to null. Safe to call on an
already-null slot.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle *conn
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_interrupt`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Interrupts the query currently executing on the connection.

The cross-thread (but not cross-connection) cancellation entry point
for streaming results: safe to call from any thread within the execution
of a query through a connection, including while another thread steps
the query's result. A no-op when no query is active. Cancellation surfaces
on the consuming side as step status CANCELLED ([`duckdb_v2_result_step`](#duckdb_v2_result_step)), or as
ERROR_RUNTIME_INTERRUPT ([`duckdb_v2_result_fetch_chunk`](#duckdb_v2_result_fetch_chunk)).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_interrupt(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection whose active query to interrupt.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_progress_get`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Captures a snapshot of the active query's execution progress.

Reads the percentage and row counts from one consistent snapshot
of the query currently executing on the connection. Safe to call
from any thread, including while another thread steps the query's
result.

Progress is published only when the enable_progress_bar option is
set; the bridge does not enable tracking itself. Both row counts
are 0 when no information is available. The percentage is -1 when
tracking is disabled, no query is active, or no progress has been
published yet.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_progress_get(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  double *out_percentage,
  uint64_t *out_rows_processed,
  uint64_t *out_total_rows_to_process,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection.
* `out_percentage`: Receives the percentage complete in [0, 100], -1 if tracking is disabled, no query is active, or no progress has been published yet. (out)
* `out_rows_processed`: Receives the number of rows processed so far. (out)
* `out_total_rows_to_process`: Receives the total number of rows the query will process. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Custom Type

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom type being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_create`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_create), configured with [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name) and
[`duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type), made available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type), and destroyed with
[`duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy).

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_custom_type_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_custom_type_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">base_type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_extension_handle</span> <span class="nv">extension</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">type</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_type_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new custom type through a factory.

The type starts out empty: configure it with [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name) and [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type), then
make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type). The caller
owns the returned handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy), also after registration.

The custom type can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_type_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle *type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the custom type through.
* `type`: On success, receives the newly created custom type. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the custom type.

This is the name the type is referred to by in SQL, and the alias carried by every logical type instance of
it. The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name. A name must be set
before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle type,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The type to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the base type of the custom type.

The custom type shares the base type's internal representation but is logically distinct, so it can carry
its own cast functions. The type is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous base type.
A base type must be set before registration, and it must be a fully defined concrete type -- ANY is a
signature wildcard, not something a registered type can be built on.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_type_set_base_type(
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle base_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The type to set the base type of.
* `base_type`: The logical type to base the custom type on. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the custom type, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The type is registered on the connection's database, visible to every connection, in the connection's transaction:
inside an explicit transaction, it is invisible to other connections until the transaction commits, and a rollback
undoes it. Registration requires a name and a complete base type. The custom type must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy), which does not affect the registered type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_type(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `type`: The custom type to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the custom type, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The type is registered on the loading extension's database and attributed to the extension. Use this from the
extension's load callback. Registration requires a name and a complete base type. The custom type must have been
created through a factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must
destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy), which does not affect the registered type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_type(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `type`: The custom type to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the custom type, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_type_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_custom_type_handle *type
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The type to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Data Chunk

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">types</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">column_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_chunk</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_copy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_copy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_chunk</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> *<span class="nv">chunk</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_clear"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_clear</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_size"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_size</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_size</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_capacity"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_capacity</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_capacity</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle</span> <span class="nv">chunk</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_vector_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_vector</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates an empty data chunk with the given column types, drawing its allocator from a factory.

The chunk's vectors are allocated through the factory's database, so the
memory is accounted to that database. Allocates one FLAT vector per element of the
types array, each at default capacity. Every vector starts at size 0; set
it with vector_set_size once the vector is populated. The chunk is
caller-owned and must be destroyed via data_chunk_destroy.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  const duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *types,
  idx_t column_count,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle *out_chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create with.
* `types`: Pointer to an array of logical_type handles, one per column.
* `column_count`: Number of elements in the types array.
* `out_chunk`: Receives the new chunk handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_copy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a deep copy of a data chunk, drawing its allocator from a factory.

Allocates a new chunk with the source chunk's column types and copies all rows into it, through the factory's database. The copy is flattened and owns all its data, so it stays valid after the source chunk or whatever backs it (such as a column data collection scan state) is destroyed. The returned chunk is caller-owned and must be destroyed via data_chunk_destroy.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_copy(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle *out_chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create with.
* `chunk`: The chunk to copy. Left unchanged.
* `out_chunk`: Receives the new chunk handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a data chunk handle.

Null-safe: passing nullptr or a slot already set to nullptr is a no-op.
On success the slot is set to nullptr. Any vector previously borrowed
from this chunk becomes invalid.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle *chunk
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_clear`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Empties a data chunk so it can be filled again.

The chunk's size becomes 0, and each of its vectors becomes a writable FLAT vector of its type again, as on
creation, so a chunk can be reused for one batch after another instead of being created for each. Data, views
and pointers taken from the chunk or its vectors beforehand do not survive this. Must not be called on a chunk
DuckDB lends to a callback for reading.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_clear(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk to clear.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_size`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the row count of a data chunk.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_size(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  idx_t *out_size,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk.
* `out_size`: Receives the row count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_capacity`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of rows a data chunk can hold, e.g. how many rows the exec callback of a table function may
write into its output chunk in one call.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_capacity(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  idx_t *out_capacity,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk.
* `out_capacity`: Receives the number of rows the chunk can hold. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of vectors in a data chunk.

Equals the column count of the producing result.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector_count(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk.
* `out_count`: Receives the vector count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the vector at the given index in a data chunk.

The returned handle is borrowed and valid until the chunk is destroyed;
do not destroy it. An out-of-range index returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector(
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle chunk,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_vector_handle *out_vector,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `chunk`: The chunk.
* `index`: The vector index, in [0, vector_count).
* `out_vector`: Receives the borrowed vector handle. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Environment

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_environment_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_environment_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_environment_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_env</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_environment_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_environment_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_environment_handle</span> *<span class="nv">env</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_environment_get_instance_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_environment_get_instance_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_environment_handle</span> <span class="nv">env</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_environment_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates the V2 environment. Call once at program start.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_environment_create(
  duckdb_v2_environment_handle *out_env,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `out_env`: Receives the new environment handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_environment_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the environment.

Refuses with ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE while any instance created through
this environment is still alive; destroy those instances first, then
retry. On success the handle is set to null.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_environment_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_environment_handle *env
);
```

##### Parameters

* `env`: The environment.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_environment_get_instance_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of instances currently alive under the environment.

A diagnostic accessor, for tracking down leaked instances when
[`duckdb_v2_environment_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_environment_destroy) returns ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE. The count is a
snapshot and may change before the next call.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_environment_get_instance_count(
  duckdb_v2_environment_handle env,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `env`: The environment.
* `out_count`: Receives the number of live instances. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_error_info_get_raw_text"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_error_info_get_raw_text</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">out_raw_text</span>);

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_get_code`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the error code associated with an error info handle.

On success, writes the info's error code to `*out_code`. On failure
(e.g. if `info` is invalid), leaves `*out_code` unchanged and returns
a non-success error code.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_get_code(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle info,
  DUCKDB_V2_ERROR *out_code
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to query.
* `out_code`: The error code associated with the info, if the call succeeds. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_get_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the error text associated with an error info handle.

Returns a borrowed pointer to the info's null-terminated error text.
The pointer is owned by DuckDB and is valid until the info is destroyed 
or a new text is set; callers must not free it, and must not read it once 
the info has been destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_get_text(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_str *out_text
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to query.
* `out_text`: Receives a borrowed view of the text. Owned by DuckDB; valid until the info handle is destroyed. (out, borrowed)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_get_raw_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the error text body without the leading category prefix.

Returns a borrowed view of the same text error_info_get_text reports,
minus the leading “`<Type>` Error: ” prefix. This is the authoritative
unprefixed body: the API exposes no type name, so the prefix cannot be
reconstructed and the body cannot be derived from error_info_get_text.
Unprefixed does not mean plain — the body keeps whatever form it was
rendered in (a LINE/caret block by default, JSON under errors_as_json).
`{NULL, 0}` when there is no text. The pointer is owned by DuckDB and
valid until the info handle is destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_get_raw_text(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_str *out_raw_text
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to query.
* `out_raw_text`: Receives a borrowed view of the raw text. Owned by DuckDB; valid until the info handle is destroyed. (out, borrowed)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_set_code`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the error code for an error info handle.

On success, replaces the info's error code with the provided one. On
failure, nothing is changed. Accepts a `nullptr` info handle, in which
case the call is a no-op and returns ERROR_NONE.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_set_code(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle info,
  DUCKDB_V2_ERROR code
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to set. On success, updated with the provided code.
* `code`: The error code to set in the info.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_set_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the error text for an error info handle.

On success, replaces the info's text with the provided one; DuckDB
allocates its own copy of the string. On failure, nothing is changed.
Accepts a `nullptr` info handle, in which case the call is a no-op and
returns ERROR_NONE.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_set_text(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_str *text
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to set. On success, updated with the provided text.
* `text`: The error text to set in the info.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys an error info handle and frees its resources.

Null-safe: calling with a null handle, or a null pointer-to-handle, is a
no-op and returns ERROR_NONE. On return `*info` is set to nullptr. Safe
to call on any info DuckDB returned.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *info
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The error info handle to destroy. Set to nullptr on return.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Extension

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_get_api_fn`

Hands back the function-pointer table for the API version the extension
was built against, or NULL if this DuckDB cannot serve it.

The extension calls it exactly once, first, through
DUCKDB_EXTENSION_API_INIT; nothing else in the API may be called before
it succeeds. A NULL return means the load has already failed and DuckDB
has recorded why, so the entrypoint must return without touching the
error slot. Statically linked extensions resolve DuckDB's symbols at link
time and never call it, so for those the field is NULL.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef const void *(*duckdb_v2_extension_get_api_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  const char *version
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The extension being loaded, as handed to the entrypoint.
* `version`: The API version the extension was built against, e.g. “v2.0.0”.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_input`

The single argument to a V2 C extension entrypoint. Borrowed for the
duration of the call: none of its fields outlive the entrypoint, and the
extension destroys none of them.

##### Fields

* `get_api` (`duckdb_v2_extension_get_api_fn`): Fetches the versioned function-pointer table. NULL for a statically linked extension.
* `extension` (`duckdb_v2_extension_handle`): The extension being loaded, and the token get_api takes.
* `context` (`duckdb_v2_context_handle`): A borrowed context to read and run queries through, with a transaction
already active. Valid only until the extension entrypoint returns; do
not retain or destroy it.
* `err` (`duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *`): A live error slot: never NULL, and never pointing at NULL. Populate it
with error_info_set_code, and optionally error_info_set_text, to fail
the load. Do not destroy it -- DuckDB owns it. Pass a slot of your own
to calls whose failure you intend to handle, so only a failure you
mean to abort the load with lands here.

<br>

### Factory

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_context_get_factory"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_context_get_factory</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_context_handle</span> <span class="nv">ctx</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_factory</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the factory of an instance.

The factory creates the built-in types and their values, casts with the
built-in casts only, and allocates data chunks and column data
collections through the instance.
Anything that needs a catalog — catalog-registered types, qualified type
names — returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. The returned handle is borrowed: it
is valid for as long as the instance is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_get_factory(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle *out_factory,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance.
* `out_factory`: Receives the borrowed factory. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the factory of a connection.

The factory reaches the connection's catalog and settings. Catalog
lookups run in the connection's active transaction, or in a transaction
of their own when none is open; nothing else opens a transaction. The
returned handle is borrowed: it is valid for as long as the connection
is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_get_factory(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle *out_factory,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection.
* `out_factory`: Receives the borrowed factory. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_context_get_factory`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the factory of a context.

The factory reaches the context's catalog and settings, within the
transaction the context already has. The returned handle is borrowed:
it is valid for as long as the context is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_context_get_factory(
  duckdb_v2_context_handle ctx,
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle *out_factory,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `ctx`: The context.
* `out_factory`: Receives the borrowed factory. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### File System

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to a file system. Obtained from [`duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system`](#duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system),
[`duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system) or [`duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system), and used to open files with
[`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open). Borrowed: the handle belongs to the instance, connection or context it came from, is
valid only for as long as that is, and must not be destroyed.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle`

An owned opaque handle to the options a file is opened with. Created with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create),
configured with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag) and [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value), passed to
[`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy). One options object can open any number
of files, and destroying it does not affect files already opened with it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_handle`

An owned opaque handle to an open file, produced by [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) and destroyed with
[`duckdb_v2_file_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_destroy). Read, write, seek and sync through the `file_*` functions. Only usable while the file
system it was opened through is still valid.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob_callback_fn`

Receives one path matched by [`duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob).

The view is borrowed for the duration of the call only, and is not guaranteed to be null-terminated. Report an
error through `err`, a live slot that must not be destroyed, to stop the glob: [`duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob) then fails
with that error. The callback must not throw or unwind across the boundary.

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob_callback_fn)(
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  void *user_data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `path`: Borrowed view of the matched path. Valid only until the callback returns.
* `user_data`: The pointer passed to [`duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob), untouched.
* `err`: A live error slot to report a failure through, which stops the glob.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG`

How [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) opens a file. These are not a bitmask -- apply
them one at a time with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag), calling it once
per behaviour you want, e.g. `FILE_FLAG_WRITE` then `FILE_FLAG_CREATE` to
write to a file and create it when it does not exist.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_INVALID` = 0: Not a flag. The zero value, so that an uninitialized variable does not name a behaviour; applying it is an error.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_READ` = 1: Open the file with “read” capabilities.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_WRITE` = 2: Open the file with “write” capabilities.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_CREATE` = 3: Create the file if it does not exist, and open it as it is if it does.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_CREATE_NEW` = 4: Create the file if it does not exist, and truncate it to empty if it does. To fail instead of truncating, combine `FILE_FLAG_CREATE` with `FILE_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE_CREATE`.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_APPEND` = 5: Open the file in “append” mode.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE_CREATE` = 6: Fail if the file already exists. A modifier on `FILE_FLAG_CREATE`, and meaningless without it.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_PARALLEL_ACCESS` = 7: The file will be read and written at explicit offsets from several threads at once. Pass it whenever
[`duckdb_v2_file_read_at`](#duckdb_v2_file_read_at) or [`duckdb_v2_file_write_at`](#duckdb_v2_file_write_at) are used concurrently -- a file system that would otherwise
assume sequential access, by caching, buffering, or keeping a single cursor, needs to know not to.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG_EXTERNAL_FILE_CACHE` = 8: Read the file through DuckDB's external file cache, which keeps the bytes that were read in memory, so
that later reads of the same file - also by later queries - do not have to read them again. Whether a
local file is cached is decided by the `cache_local_files` setting. Only meaningful for reading.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_context_handle</span> <span class="nv">context</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_system_handle</span> *<span class="nv">file_system</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_system_handle</span> *<span class="nv">file_system</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_system_handle</span> *<span class="nv">file_system</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_system_handle</span> <span class="nv">file_system</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle</span> *<span class="nv">options</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle</span> <span class="nv">options</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG</span> <span class="nv">flag</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

#### `duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the file system of a context.

The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid only for as long as the context is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system(
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle *file_system,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `context`: The context to take the file system from.
* `file_system`: Receives the borrowed file system. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the file system of an instance.

Paths are resolved with the instance's GLOBAL settings and secrets, and file I/O is not attributed to any query.

The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid only for as long as the instance is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_get_file_system(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle *file_system,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance to take the file system from.
* `file_system`: Receives the borrowed file system. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the file system of a connection.

Paths are resolved with the connection's settings and secrets, and file I/O is attributed to its running query, as through [`duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system`](#duckdb_v2_context_get_file_system) in a callback.

The returned handle is borrowed: it is valid only for as long as the connection is, and must not be destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_get_file_system(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle *file_system,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to take the file system from.
* `file_system`: Receives the borrowed file system. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a set of open options for a file system.

The options start out empty: give them flags with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag), which is required, and
optionally attach values with [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value). They are then passed to [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open),
and can be reused for as many opens as you like. The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy).

The options belong to the file system they were created from, since which values mean anything depends on
which file system ends up handling the path.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle *options,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system the options are for.
* `options`: On success, receives the new options. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Applies one flag to the options.

Additive: call it once per behaviour you want, and applying the same flag twice is harmless. At least one
flag must be applied before the options can open anything, since the flags are what say whether the file is
being read or written. There is no way to take a flag back -- build a fresh set of options instead.

`FILE_FLAG_INVALID` names no behaviour and is rejected, as is any value that is not a [`DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG`](#duckdb_v2_file_flag).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_flag(
  duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle options,
  DUCKDB_V2_FILE_FLAG flag,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `options`: The options to apply the flag to.
* `flag`: The flag to apply.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Attaches a named value to the options.

These are hints for whichever file system ends up handling the path, and what they mean is that file system's
business: a value it does not recognise is ignored rather than rejected, and the same name can mean different
things to different file systems. They are the same values a file system reports when listing files, so a
known file size or modification time learned from a listing can be handed straight back to avoid re-reading
it.

The name and the value are borrowed and copied, so the caller may destroy the value immediately after.
Setting the same name again replaces the previous value. Names are case-sensitive.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_open_options_set_value(
  duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle options,
  const duckdb_v2_str *name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `options`: The options to set the value on.
* `name`: The name of the value. Borrowed and copied.
* `value`: The value. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the options, releasing their resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Files already opened with these options are unaffected.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_open_options_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle *options
);
```

##### Parameters

* `options`: The options to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_open`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Opens a file.

Opens the file at the given path through the file system, which routes it the way the engine would -- a path
handled by a registered virtual or remote file system goes there rather than to local disk. The returned
handle is owned by the caller and must be destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_file_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_destroy).

The options carry the flags and any file-system-specific values; see [`duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create`](#duckdb_v2_file_open_options_create). Opening
without having set flags fails, since the flags are what say whether the file is being read or written.

Failure to open -- a missing file without `FILE_FLAG_CREATE`, insufficient permissions, an existing file
under `FILE_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE_CREATE` -- is reported as an error.

Flag combinations that contradict each other, such as naming neither read nor write or combining
`FILE_FLAG_CREATE` with `FILE_FLAG_CREATE_NEW`, are a programming error rather than a supported input. An
assertion build catches them; elsewhere the behaviour is whatever the underlying file system does with them.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_open(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *file_path,
  duckdb_v2_file_open_options_handle options,
  duckdb_v2_file_handle *file,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system to open the file through.
* `file_path`: The path of the file to open. Borrowed for the call only.
* `options`: How to open the file. Borrowed for the call only, and reusable across opens.
* `file`: On success, receives the open file. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_file_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_exists`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reports whether a file exists at the given path.

The path is routed the way [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) routes it, so asking about a path handled by a remote file
system may reach out to it. A directory is not a file, and reports false.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_exists(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  bool *out_exists,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system to ask.
* `path`: The path to check. Borrowed for the call only.
* `out_exists`: Receives whether a file exists at the path. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_is_remote`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reports whether a path names a remote file, e.g. one under `s3://`, `https://`, `gcs://` or `azure://`.

Decided from the path alone: no file system is consulted, so it answers even when the extension providing the
remote file system is not loaded.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_is_remote(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  bool *out_is_remote,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system the path is meant for.
* `path`: The path to check. Borrowed for the call only.
* `out_is_remote`: Receives whether the path names a remote file. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_expand`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Expands a path as the file system does when opening it: a leading `~` becomes the home directory, as the
`home_directory` setting configures it.

A path without anything to expand is handed back as it is. The expanded path is handed to `sink` in a single
call.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_expand(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  duckdb_v2_text_sink_fn sink,
  void *user_data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system whose settings expand the path.
* `path`: The path to expand. Borrowed for the call only.
* `sink`: Receives the expanded path in a single call. Borrowed for the duration of that call; see text_sink for the full contract.
* `user_data`: Opaque pointer passed through to sink untouched. May be NULL.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Finds the files matching a glob pattern, e.g. `*.csv` or `data_?.json` in a directory, handing each matched path to
`callback`.

The pattern is routed the way [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) routes a path, so globbing a remote path may reach out to
the file system handling it, and is only supported where that file system supports it. A pattern without glob
characters matches the file it names, if there is one. Matching nothing is not an error. In which order the
paths are handed over is up to the file system.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *pattern,
  duckdb_v2_file_system_path_glob_callback_fn callback,
  void *user_data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system to glob in.
* `pattern`: The glob pattern. Borrowed for the call only.
* `callback`: Invoked once per matched path.
* `user_data`: Opaque pointer passed through to `callback` untouched. May be NULL.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_move`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Moves, or renames, a file from one path to another.

The move is handled by the file system `source` routes to, the way [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) routes a path; moving
a file between two file systems is not supported. Whether an existing file at `target` is replaced, and whether
the move is atomic, is up to that file system.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_move(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *source,
  const duckdb_v2_str *target,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system to move the file in.
* `source`: The path of the file to move. Borrowed for the call only.
* `target`: The path to move the file to. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_system_path_remove`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Removes the file at a path, if there is one.

The path is routed the way [`duckdb_v2_file_system_open`](#duckdb_v2_file_system_open) routes it. A path with no file is not an error: `out_removed`
then receives false. A file that exists but cannot be removed is.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_system_path_remove(
  duckdb_v2_file_system_handle file_system,
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  bool *out_removed,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file_system`: The file system to remove the file from.
* `path`: The path of the file to remove. Borrowed for the call only.
* `out_removed`: Optional. Receives whether a file was removed. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_read`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reads from the file into a caller-supplied buffer.

Reads up to `buffer_size` bytes from the file's current position, advancing it by however many were read.
Fewer bytes than asked for is normal at the end of the file, and zero means there is nothing left; neither is
an error. The file must have been opened with `FILE_FLAG_READ`.

Use [`duckdb_v2_file_read_at`](#duckdb_v2_file_read_at) to read at an explicit offset instead, which leaves the position alone and so can run
on several threads at once.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_read(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  void *buffer,
  idx_t buffer_size,
  idx_t *bytes_read,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to read from.
* `buffer`: A caller-owned buffer of at least `buffer_size` bytes, receiving what was read.
* `buffer_size`: The maximum number of bytes to read.
* `bytes_read`: Receives how many bytes were actually read, which may be fewer than `buffer_size` at the end of the file. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_write`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes a caller-supplied buffer to the file.

Writes up to `buffer_size` bytes at the file's current position, advancing it by however many were written.
The file must have been opened with `FILE_FLAG_WRITE` or `FILE_FLAG_APPEND`. Writes may be buffered; use
[`duckdb_v2_file_sync`](#duckdb_v2_file_sync) to force them out.

Use [`duckdb_v2_file_write_at`](#duckdb_v2_file_write_at) to write at an explicit offset instead, which leaves the position alone and so can run
on several threads at once.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_write(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  const void *buffer,
  idx_t buffer_size,
  idx_t *bytes_written,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to write to.
* `buffer`: A caller-owned buffer of at least `buffer_size` bytes, holding what to write.
* `buffer_size`: The number of bytes to write.
* `bytes_written`: Receives how many bytes were actually written. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_read_at`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reads from a fixed offset, without moving the file's position.

Reads exactly `buffer_size` bytes starting at `location`. Unlike [`duckdb_v2_file_read`](#duckdb_v2_file_read), a short read is an error
rather than a result: reaching the end of the file before `buffer_size` bytes fails, so there is no count to
report back. The file's read/write position is untouched, which is what makes this safe to call from several
threads at once -- provided the file was opened with `FILE_FLAG_PARALLEL_ACCESS`.

The file must have been opened with `FILE_FLAG_READ`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_read_at(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  void *buffer,
  idx_t buffer_size,
  idx_t location,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to read from.
* `buffer`: A caller-owned buffer of at least `buffer_size` bytes, receiving what was read.
* `buffer_size`: The number of bytes to read. All of them are read, or the call fails.
* `location`: The absolute byte offset to read from, measured from the start of the file.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_write_at`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes at a fixed offset, without moving the file's position.

Writes exactly `buffer_size` bytes starting at `location`, extending the file when the offset is past its end.
Unlike [`duckdb_v2_file_write`](#duckdb_v2_file_write) there is no count to report back: all of the bytes are written, or the call fails. The
file's read/write position is untouched, which is what makes this safe to call from several threads at once --
provided the file was opened with `FILE_FLAG_PARALLEL_ACCESS`, and that the threads write disjoint ranges.

The file must have been opened with `FILE_FLAG_WRITE`. Writes may be buffered; use [`duckdb_v2_file_sync`](#duckdb_v2_file_sync) to force
them out.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_write_at(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  const void *buffer,
  idx_t buffer_size,
  idx_t location,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to write to.
* `buffer`: A caller-owned buffer of at least `buffer_size` bytes, holding what to write.
* `buffer_size`: The number of bytes to write. All of them are written, or the call fails.
* `location`: The absolute byte offset to write at, measured from the start of the file.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_tell`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the file's current read/write position, as a byte offset from the start of the file.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_tell(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  idx_t *position,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to query.
* `position`: Receives the current position, as a byte offset from the start of the file. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_size`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the total size of the file in bytes.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_size(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  idx_t *size,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to query.
* `size`: Receives the total size of the file in bytes. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_seek`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Moves the file's read/write position.

Sets the position to an absolute byte offset from the start of the file; subsequent reads and writes start
there. Seeking past the end is allowed, and reading from there yields nothing.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_seek(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  idx_t position,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to seek within.
* `position`: The absolute byte offset to seek to, measured from the start of the file.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_sync`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Flushes buffered writes to persistent storage.

Forces anything still buffered out to storage, which is what makes writes durable across a crash or a
process exit. Closing or destroying the handle flushes as well.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_sync(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to synchronize.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_close`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Closes the file without destroying the handle.

Releases the operating-system resources behind the file, such as its descriptor. The handle itself stays
valid and must still be destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_file_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_file_destroy), but it can no longer read, write or seek.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_close(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle file,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to close.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_file_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the file, closing it if it is still open.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_file_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_file_handle *file
);
```

##### Parameters

* `file`: The file to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Function

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the call site a bind callback is binding. Every function family's bind callback
receives this handle next to its own bind info. It gives access to the arguments of the call, the function's
user data, and the bind data.

The arguments form one list in four parts, in this order: one argument per positional-only and standard
parameter, in declaration order; the arguments `*args` received, in call order; one argument per named-only
parameter, in declaration order; and the arguments `**kwargs` received, in call order. How the caller passed an
argument does not matter: a standard parameter passed by name is at its declared position. A parameter the call
omitted is present with its default value. See [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count) for the size of each part.

<br>
