#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the user data set on the function being bound, e.g. via [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_user_data).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `data`: Receives the user data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_set_bind_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the function's “bind data” from the bind callback.

The bind data is stored with the bound call site and retrievable from every later callback. The opaque
handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor, invoked when the bind data is no longer needed,
and an optional equality callback used when comparing two bound call sites; without one, pointer equality
is used. Scalar functions set their bind data through [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_set_bind_data`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_set_bind_data) instead.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_set_bind_data(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the bind data pointer plus optional destructor and equality callbacks.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of arguments of the call site being bound, split into the four parts of the argument list.

The parts follow each other in this order: the positional-only and standard parameters, the arguments `*args`
received, the named-only parameters, and the arguments `**kwargs` received. The argument at index `i` of the
named-only part is therefore at index `positional_fixed + positional_variadic + i`. Valid indices for the
other argument functions are [0, the sum of the four counts). Every out-parameter may be NULL, in which case
nothing is written to it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  idx_t *positional_fixed,
  idx_t *positional_variadic,
  idx_t *named_fixed,
  idx_t *named_variadic,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `positional_fixed`: Optional. Receives the number of positional-only and standard parameters. (out)
* `positional_variadic`: Optional. Receives the number of arguments `*args` received, 0 when the signature has none. (out)
* `named_fixed`: Optional. Receives the number of named-only parameters. (out)
* `named_variadic`: Optional. Receives the number of arguments `**kwargs` received, 0 when the signature has none. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the type of the argument at the given index.

Fails if the index is out of bounds. The returned type is owned by the caller and must be destroyed via
[`duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_type(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `index`: The index of the argument.
* `type`: Receives the argument type. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Folds the argument at the given index to a constant value.

Fails if the argument is not constant, e.g. a column reference, or if the index is out of bounds. The
arguments of a table or pragma function are always constant. The resulting value may be NULL. The returned value is
owned by the caller and must be destroyed via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_value(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `index`: The index of the argument.
* `value`: Receives the constant value. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the name of the argument at the given index.

For an argument of a declared parameter, this is the parameter name. For an argument `**kwargs` received, it
is the name the caller passed, which may be the name of a positional-only parameter. An argument `*args`
received has no name, and yields an empty name. Fails if the index is out of bounds. The name is borrowed
and valid only for the duration of the callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_name(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `index`: The index of the argument.
* `name`: Receives a borrowed view of the argument name. Valid only for the duration of the callback. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_index`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Looks up the index of an argument by name.

Names are matched case-insensitively, against the names a caller can pass an argument by: those of the
standard and named-only parameters, and those `**kwargs` received. Positional-only parameters are skipped,
so `f(1, x := 2)` with a positional-only `x` finds the argument `**kwargs` received. A name the call did not
pass is not an error: `found` receives false and `index` is left untouched. A standard or named-only
parameter is always found, as the call either passed it or it carries its default value.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_index(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  idx_t *index,
  bool *found,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `name`: The name to look up. Borrowed for the call only.
* `index`: Receives the index of the argument, if found. (out)
* `found`: Receives whether the call has an argument of that name. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Function Docs

#### `duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the documentation of a function overload. Taken from the function it documents with
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_docs`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_docs), [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_docs`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_docs), [`duckdb_v2_table_function_get_docs`](#duckdb_v2_table_function_get_docs),
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_docs`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_docs) or [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs), and valid for as long as that function handle is; the caller never destroys it.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle</span> <span class="nv">docs</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">description</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle</span> <span class="nv">docs</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">title</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">example</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle</span> <span class="nv">docs</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">category</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the description of the function overload.

The description is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous description.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description(
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle docs,
  const duckdb_v2_str *description,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `docs`: The documentation to set the description of.
* `description`: The description to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Adds an example of calling the function overload.

The title and the example are borrowed and copied, and examples are reported in the order they were added.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example(
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle docs,
  const duckdb_v2_str *title,
  const duckdb_v2_str *example,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `docs`: The documentation to add the example to.
* `title`: Optional. The title of the example; NULL or an empty view for none. Borrowed and copied.
* `example`: The example, e.g. a SQL expression calling the function. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Adds a category the function overload belongs to, e.g. “string” or “aggregate”.

The category is borrowed and copied, and categories are reported in the order they were added.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category(
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle docs,
  const duckdb_v2_str *category,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `docs`: The documentation to add the category to.
* `category`: The category. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Function Signature

#### `duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle`

An opaque handle to a function signature. Carries the function's parameters and return type.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND`

How a caller passes the argument for a parameter, following Python's parameter kinds. A signature orders its
parameters by kind, in the order the values are listed here. Pass one of these to
[`duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter`](#duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter).

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_POSITIONAL_ONLY` = 0: Passed by position only. The name is invisible to a caller: a named argument with the same name is received
by `**kwargs`, or rejected when the signature has none.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_STANDARD` = 1: Passed by position or by name.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_POSITIONAL_VARIADIC` = 2: `*args`: receives the positional arguments left over after the positional-only and standard parameters,
each cast to the parameter type. ANY leaves them un-cast.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_NAMED_ONLY` = 3: Passed by name only.
* `DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_NAMED_VARIADIC` = 4: `**kwargs`: receives the named arguments that match no other parameter, each cast to the parameter type.
ANY leaves them un-cast.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle</span> <span class="nv">sig</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_value_handle</span> <span class="nv">value</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND</span> <span class="nv">kind</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle</span> <span class="nv">sig</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Adds a parameter to a signature.

The kind decides how a caller passes the argument; see [`DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND`](#duckdb_v2_function_parameter_kind). The signature keeps its
parameters ordered by kind, and parameters of the same kind in the order they were added, so parameters of
different kinds can be added in any order. A default value makes the parameter optional; `*args` and
`**kwargs` cannot have one.

Registration fails when two parameters share a name, when the signature has more than one `*args` or
`**kwargs` parameter, or when a standard parameter without a default value follows one with a default value.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter(
  duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle sig,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND kind,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sig`: The signature to configure.
* `name`: The parameter name. Borrowed and copied.
* `type`: The parameter type. ANY accepts an argument of any type without casting it. Borrowed and copied.
* `value`: Optional default value, borrowed and copied. Will be cast to the parameter type.
* `kind`: How a caller passes the argument for the parameter.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the return type of a signature.

Sets the signature's return type. The type is borrowed and copied.
Calling this again overwrites the previous return type. An INVALID
type is rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. Whether a concrete return
type is required, and whether ANY is accepted, depends on the function
family and is enforced when the signature is registered with a builder.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type(
  duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle sig,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sig`: The signature to configure.
* `type`: The return type. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Identifier

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_identifier_render_quoted"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_identifier_render_quoted</span></a>(<span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">char</span> *<span class="nv">out_text</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">out_capacity</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_length</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_identifier_render_quoted`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Renders a name as a SQL identifier, quoting and escaping only when required.

Produces the SQL text for the name: the name itself when it is already a legal bare identifier, or the name
double-quoted with interior double quotes doubled when it is a keyword or contains characters that require
quoting. This is the engine's own identifier rendering, so the result parses back to a name equal to the
input.

Writes into a caller-supplied buffer, so nothing is allocated on the caller's behalf and nothing has to be
freed. Pass out_text = NULL to size the buffer without rendering into it: out_length then receives the length,
and out_capacity is ignored. With out_text != NULL, out_capacity must be at least out_length + 1, or the call
returns ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE with out_length set to the required length and out_text left untouched.

out_length never counts the terminator, but a successful write always appends one, so the buffer is usable as
a C string.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_identifier_render_quoted(
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  char *out_text,
  idx_t out_capacity,
  idx_t *out_length,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The name to render. Borrowed for the call only.
* `out_text`: Caller-owned buffer receiving the text plus a null terminator, or NULL to only report the required length in out_length. (out)
* `out_capacity`: Bytes available in out_text, terminator included. Ignored when out_text is NULL.
* `out_length`: Receives the text length excluding the null terminator — written on success and on ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Instance

#### `duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to the `(KEY value)` options of one
[`duckdb_v2_instance_attach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_attach) call, as SQL `ATTACH` accepts them. Created from the
instance handle it will be used with via [`duckdb_v2_attach_options_create`](#duckdb_v2_attach_options_create); destroy
it via [`duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy).

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_environment_handle</span> <span class="nv">env</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_environment_handle</span> <span class="nv">env</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">option_names</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">option_values</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">option_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> *<span class="nv">instance</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_attach"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_attach</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">path</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle</span> <span class="nv">options</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> <span class="nv">make_default</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_detach"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_detach</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_set_default</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_attach_options_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_attach_options_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_options</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_attach_options_set"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_attach_options_set</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle</span> <span class="nv">options</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">key</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">setting</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates an instance under the environment with no startup options.

The instance is ready on return, with no database attached: attach one
with [`duckdb_v2_instance_attach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_attach) and pick the default with
[`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default), or connect with [`duckdb_v2_connection_create`](#duckdb_v2_connection_create).
To choose an option that cannot change once the instance exists, such
as access_mode, use [`duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options) instead. The
caller destroys the instance via [`duckdb_v2_instance_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_instance_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_create(
  duckdb_v2_environment_handle env,
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle *out_instance,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `env`: The environment.
* `out_instance`: Receives the new instance handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates an instance under the environment, configured with startup
options.

Behaves as [`duckdb_v2_instance_create`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create), applying the startup options first.

Startup options are (name, value) pairs in two parallel arrays, the
values in the textual form SQL `SET` accepts. They are the only way to
choose an option that cannot change once the instance exists, such as
access_mode or allow_unsigned_extensions; every other option can be
written now or later through [`duckdb_v2_instance_get_config`](#duckdb_v2_instance_get_config). An option that
needs a running instance (the logging options, allowed_directories,
allowed_paths, disabled_filesystems) returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID here:
write it through the instance's config after creation. A name no core
option or loaded extension defines is kept for an extension to consume
while the instance starts up, and creation fails with the names none
claimed. The caller destroys the instance via [`duckdb_v2_instance_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_instance_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options(
  duckdb_v2_environment_handle env,
  const duckdb_v2_str *option_names,
  const duckdb_v2_str *option_values,
  idx_t option_count,
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle *out_instance,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `env`: The environment.
* `option_names`: Optional. An array of option_count option names (canonical or alias). Pass NULL when option_count is 0.
* `option_values`: Optional. An array of option_count values, parallel to option_names, in the textual form SQL `SET` accepts. Pass NULL when option_count is 0.
* `option_count`: The number of startup options.
* `out_instance`: Receives the new instance handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the instance handle.

Always succeeds. Every attached database is closed with the instance.
The instance itself stays alive for as long as any connection still
references it; when the last reference drops, it is destroyed and its
database files become available to open again. On success the handle
is set to null. Safe to call on an already-null slot.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle *instance
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance handle to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_attach`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Attaches a database to the instance.

Attaches the database at `path` exactly like `ATTACH 'path'`:
  * `:memory:` or an empty view attaches a fresh in-memory database.
  * any other path attaches that file, creating it if it does not
    exist.
`name` is the name to attach under, like `ATTACH ... AS name`; it is
how [`duckdb_v2_instance_detach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_detach) and [`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default) refer to the
database. Null, or an empty view, derives the name from the path the
way SQL `ATTACH` without `AS` does:
  * `memory` for `:memory:` or an empty view;
  * otherwise the file name up to its first `.`, without any `?query`
    parameters (`/data/sales.2024.db` attaches as `sales`), with
    `_db` appended when that is a reserved name such as `system` or
    `temp`.
Naming is how two files with the same base name, or `:memory:` twice,
attach side by side. `options`
may be null; it carries the `(KEY value)` options of SQL `ATTACH`, for
per-database options such as READ_ONLY, BLOCK_SIZE or ENCRYPTION_KEY,
and must have been created from this instance handle. `make_default`
makes the attached
database the default for connections created afterwards, exactly as a
[`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default) call right after the attach would; otherwise the
default is left alone. A path that is already attached on this or any
other instance of the environment returns ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE, and a
name that is already attached fails. Options that only apply at startup
are passed to [`duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options`](#duckdb_v2_instance_create_with_options).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_attach(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  const duckdb_v2_str *path,
  duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle options,
  bool make_default,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance handle.
* `name`: Optional. The name to attach under; null or an empty view for the name derived from the path. Borrowed and copied.
* `path`: Path to the database file, or `:memory:` / an empty view for an in-memory database.
* `options`: Optional attach options created from `instance`, or null to attach with defaults under the derived name.
* `make_default`: Whether to make the attached database the default for connections created afterwards.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_detach`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Detaches the database attached under `name`.

Detaches it like `DETACH`, checkpointing a file database first. Unlike
SQL, the default database may be detached too; new connections then
start without a default until [`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default) names another, and
existing connections bound to it keep it alive until their transaction
on it ends and fail unqualified DDL afterwards. Returns
ERROR_INPUT_INVALID when no database is attached under that name.
Connections that still reference the database keep it alive until they
release it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_detach(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance handle.
* `name`: The name the database is attached under. Borrowed.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Makes the database attached under `name` the default database for
connections created from now on.

A connection binds to the default database when it is created, so this
does not retarget existing connections: their default stays what it was
when they connected, or what they chose with `USE`. The default is where
unqualified DDL and unqualified table lookups that miss the temporary
catalog go. It stays the default for new connections until another
[`duckdb_v2_instance_set_default`](#duckdb_v2_instance_set_default) call or until it is detached; a connection whose
default has been detached fails unqualified DDL with a message saying
so until it selects another with `USE`. Returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID when
no database is attached under that name.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_set_default(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance handle.
* `name`: The name the database is attached under. Borrowed.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_attach_options_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates an empty set of attach options for use with [`duckdb_v2_instance_attach`](#duckdb_v2_instance_attach) on
`instance`.

Starts empty. The caller destroys it via [`duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy); the
options may be destroyed as soon as the attach call returns, and reused
for further attaches before that.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_attach_options_create(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle *out_options,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance handle the options will be used with.
* `out_options`: Receives the new options handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_attach_options_set`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets one attach option, like a `(KEY value)` entry of SQL `ATTACH`.

The key is matched case-insensitively, as an unquoted SQL identifier
is. The setting is passed on as the text a quoted SQL literal would
produce: the engine casts the options it knows (READ_ONLY,
RECOVERY_MODE, TYPE, DEFAULT_TABLE, VACUUM_REBUILD_INDEXES, BLOCK_SIZE,
ENCRYPTION_KEY, ...) and hands the rest to the storage extension that
ends up owning the database, which decides what they mean. Keys must be
valid UTF-8; an unknown or ill-typed option fails the attach. Both views
are borrowed and copied. Setting the same key again replaces it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_attach_options_set(
  duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle options,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *key,
  const duckdb_v2_str *setting,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `options`: The attach options.
* `key`: The option name, e.g. READ_ONLY.
* `setting`: The option value, in the textual form a quoted SQL literal would carry.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys an attach options handle.

On success the slot is set to null. Safe to call on an already-null
slot.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_attach_options_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_attach_options_handle *options
);
```

##### Parameters

* `options`: The attach options to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_library_version`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the version of the linked DuckDB library.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_library_version(
  duckdb_v2_str *out_version,

```

##### Parameters

* `out_version`: The version string. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

### Logging

#### `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL`

Severity of a log message. Mirrors DuckDB's own log levels, and is
compared against the configured threshold: an entry below it is dropped.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_TRACE` = 10: Finest detail; off in any default configuration.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG` = 20: Diagnostic detail.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_INFO` = 30: Ordinary progress information.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_WARNING` = 40: A recoverable problem.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR` = 50: An operation failed.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL_FATAL` = 60: An unrecoverable failure.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_context_log"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_context_log</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_context_handle</span> <span class="nv">ctx</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL</span> <span class="nv">level</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">log_type</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">message</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_log"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_log</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL</span> <span class="nv">level</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">log_type</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">message</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_log"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_log</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL</span> <span class="nv">level</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">log_type</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">message</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_context_log`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes a message to DuckDB's log.

The entry is attributed to the context's connection scope, so it carries
that connection's ids. Whether it is recorded at all is up to the
database's log configuration: if logging is off, or level is below the
configured threshold, or log_type is not among the enabled types, the
call succeeds and writes nothing. An empty log_type selects the default
type. Read entries back with `SELECT * FROM duckdb_logs`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_context_log(
  duckdb_v2_context_handle ctx,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL level,
  const duckdb_v2_str *log_type,
  const duckdb_v2_str *message,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `ctx`: The context to log through.
* `level`: Severity of the message.
* `log_type`: The log type to record under, matched case-sensitively. Empty selects the default type.
* `message`: The message body. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_log`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes a message to DuckDB's log.

The entry is attributed to the database scope: it carries no connection
or query ids. Whether it is recorded at all is up to the
database's log configuration: if logging is off, or level is below the
configured threshold, or log_type is not among the enabled types, the
call succeeds and writes nothing. An empty log_type selects the default
type. Read entries back with `SELECT * FROM duckdb_logs`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_log(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL level,
  const duckdb_v2_str *log_type,
  const duckdb_v2_str *message,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance to log through.
* `level`: Severity of the message.
* `log_type`: The log type to record under, matched case-sensitively. Empty selects the default type.
* `message`: The message body. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_log`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Writes a message to DuckDB's log.

The entry is attributed to the connection scope, so it carries the
connection's ids. Whether it is recorded at all is up to the
database's log configuration: if logging is off, or level is below the
configured threshold, or log_type is not among the enabled types, the
call succeeds and writes nothing. An empty log_type selects the default
type. Read entries back with `SELECT * FROM duckdb_logs`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_log(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL level,
  const duckdb_v2_str *log_type,
  const duckdb_v2_str *message,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to log through.
* `level`: Severity of the message.
* `log_type`: The log type to record under, matched case-sensitively. Empty selects the default type.
* `message`: The message body. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

### Qualified Name

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_handle`

An owned qualified name: an ordered path of one to three non-empty identifier parts whose last element is the
object name. Construct with [`duckdb_v2_qname_parse`](#duckdb_v2_qname_parse) or [`duckdb_v2_qname_create`](#duckdb_v2_qname_create), read with [`duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count`](#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count) and
[`duckdb_v2_qname_get_part`](#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part), render back to SQL with [`duckdb_v2_qname_render`](#duckdb_v2_qname_render), compare with [`duckdb_v2_qname_equals`](#duckdb_v2_qname_equals), and destroy
with [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy). Two handles are compared with [`duckdb_v2_qname_equals`](#duckdb_v2_qname_equals), never by pointer.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_parse"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_parse</span></a>(<span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">text</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">parts</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">part_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_get_part</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">part</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_render"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_render</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">char</span> *<span class="nv">out_text</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">out_capacity</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_length</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_equals"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_equals</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">left</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">right</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> *<span class="nv">result</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_hash"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_hash</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">uint64_t</span> *<span class="nv">hash</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_qname_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_parse`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Parses SQL text into a qualified name.

Applies the engine's qualified-name rules: dots separate parts, and a double-quoted part may contain dots and
doubled interior quotes. More than three parts and an unterminated quote are rejected with the parser's own
error. Invalid UTF-8 and text without at least one non-empty part are rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`.
When the parts are already separate, build the name with [`duckdb_v2_qname_create`](#duckdb_v2_qname_create) rather than joining them and parsing
the result.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_parse(
  const duckdb_v2_str *text,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `text`: The name text to parse. Borrowed for the call only.
* `name`: On success, receives the qualified name. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a qualified name from its parts.

The parts are ordered outermost first, so the last one is the object name. Between one and three parts are
accepted -- the engine qualifies at most catalog.schema.name today -- and every part must be non-empty:
partial qualification is expressed by passing fewer parts, never by empty placeholders. Zero parts, more than
three, and an empty part are all rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. The parts are borrowed and copied.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_create(
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *parts,
  idx_t part_count,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `parts`: An array of `part_count` non-empty identifier views, outermost first.
* `part_count`: The number of parts, between one and three.
* `name`: On success, receives the qualified name. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns how many parts the qualified name has.

Always at least one. Valid indices for [`duckdb_v2_qname_get_part`](#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part) are [0, count), and the object name is the part at
count - 1.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The qualified name.
* `count`: Receives the number of parts. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_get_part`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows one part of the qualified name.

Parts are ordered outermost first, so the object name is the part at [`duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count`](#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part_count) - 1. The view
is valid until the qualified name is destroyed. An index outside [0, count) is rejected with
`ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_get_part(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *part,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The qualified name.
* `index`: Zero-based part index.
* `part`: Receives a borrowed view of the part, valid until the qualified name is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_render`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Renders the qualified name as SQL text.

Joins the parts with dots, quoting and escaping each one only where the identifier requires it, so the result
parses back through [`duckdb_v2_qname_parse`](#duckdb_v2_qname_parse) to an equal name.

Writes into a caller-supplied buffer, so nothing is allocated on the caller's behalf and nothing has to be
freed. Pass out_text = NULL to size the buffer without rendering into it: out_length then receives the length,
and out_capacity is ignored. With out_text != NULL, out_capacity must be at least out_length + 1, or the call
returns ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE with out_length set to the required length and out_text left untouched.

out_length never counts the terminator, but a successful write always appends one, so the buffer is usable as
a C string.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_render(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  char *out_text,
  idx_t out_capacity,
  idx_t *out_length,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The qualified name to render.
* `out_text`: Caller-owned buffer receiving the text plus a null terminator, or NULL to only report the required length in out_length. (out)
* `out_capacity`: Bytes available in out_text, terminator included. Ignored when out_text is NULL.
* `out_length`: Receives the text length excluding the null terminator — written on success and on ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_equals`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Compares two qualified names.

True when both have the same number of parts and every part matches case-insensitively, which is the engine's
own identifier equality: casing never distinguishes two names. This is the only way to compare names; two
handles holding equal names are still distinct pointers.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_equals(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle left,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle right,
  bool *result,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `left`: The first qualified name.
* `right`: The second qualified name.
* `result`: Receives whether the two names are equal. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_hash`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Hashes a qualified name.

Consistent with [`duckdb_v2_qname_equals`](#duckdb_v2_qname_equals): names that compare equal hash equal, casing differences included. The value
is not stable across processes or library versions, so use it for in-process lookup tables only and never
persist it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_hash(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  uint64_t *hash,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The qualified name to hash.
* `hash`: Receives the hash value. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the qualified name, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Any part views borrowed from it become dangling.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_qname_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name
);
```

##### Parameters

* `name`: The qualified name to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Query Metrics

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle`

An owned snapshot of the metrics of a query. Taken with [`duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics), read from its root
node via [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy). Later queries do not
update it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to one node of a query metrics snapshot, valid for as long as the snapshot is. Read its
name with [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name), its metrics with [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric) or by index, and
its children with [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child).

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle</span> *<span class="nv">metrics</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_enable_profiling"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_enable_profiling</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> <span class="nv">enabled</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle</span> <span class="nv">metrics</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> *<span class="nv">node</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> <span class="nv">node</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> <span class="nv">node</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> <span class="nv">node</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> *<span class="nv">child</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle</span> <span class="nv">node</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Takes a snapshot of the metrics of the last query the connection finished.

The snapshot is owned by the caller and does not change afterwards. It holds the metrics DuckDB's profiling
configuration gathered: without profiling enabled, the root node carries no metrics and has no children. A
snapshot is not promised to be complete; any metric, and any operator node, may be missing.

Fails with `ERROR_RESOURCE_IN_USE` while a query is running on the connection, i.e. while a result of it has
not yet been drained or destroyed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle *metrics,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to take the snapshot of.
* `metrics`: On success, receives the owned snapshot. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_enable_profiling`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Enables or disables profiling for the queries the connection runs from now on.

While profiling is enabled, DuckDB gathers the metrics [`duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics`](#duckdb_v2_connection_get_query_metrics) reports. Profiling also
prints the profile of every query, as configured by the `enable_profiling` and `profiling_output` options, which
by default print a query tree to the standard output: set `enable_profiling` to `no_output` to only gather the
metrics. Disabling profiling stops both.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_enable_profiling(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  bool enabled,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to enable or disable profiling for.
* `enabled`: Whether to enable profiling.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the root node of the snapshot, which describes the query as a whole. Its children, if any, describe
the operators that executed the query.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_get_root(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle metrics,
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle *node,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `metrics`: The snapshot.
* `node`: Receives the borrowed root node. Valid until the snapshot is destroyed. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the name of the node: `QUERY` for the root node, and the name of the operator, e.g. `TABLE_SCAN`, for
the other nodes.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_name(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  duckdb_v2_str *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `name`: Receives a borrowed view of the name. Valid until the snapshot is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of children of the node. Valid indices for [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child) are
[0, count).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child_count(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `count`: Receives the number of children. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the child of the node at index. An out-of-range index is rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_child(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle *child,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `index`: Zero-based child index.
* `child`: Receives the borrowed child. Valid until the snapshot is destroyed. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of metrics the node carries. Valid indices for [`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_name`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_name) and
[`duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_value`](#duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_value) are [0, count); the order of the metrics is unspecified.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_count(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `count`: Receives the number of metrics. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the name of the metric at index, e.g. `query.total_time`. An out-of-range index is rejected with
`ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_name(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_str *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `index`: Zero-based metric index.
* `name`: Receives a borrowed view of the name. Valid until the snapshot is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the value of the metric at index, a number such as a UBIGINT count or a DOUBLE duration. An
out-of-range index is rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric_value(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `index`: Zero-based metric index.
* `value`: Receives the owned value. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Looks up a metric of the node by name, e.g. `query.total_time`. When the node does not carry it, `present`
receives false and `value` receives null.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_get_metric(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_node_handle node,
  const duckdb_v2_str *name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  bool *present,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `node`: The node.
* `name`: The name of the metric, matched exactly. Borrowed for the call only.
* `value`: Receives the owned value, if present. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). (out)
* `present`: Receives whether the node carries the metric. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the snapshot, releasing its resources and invalidating the nodes borrowed from it.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_query_metrics_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_query_metrics_handle *metrics
);
```

##### Parameters

* `metrics`: The snapshot to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`
