### Schema

#### `duckdb_v2_schema_handle`

An owned, ordered list of (name, type) fields. Read with schema_get_count
and schema_get_field. Destroy via schema_destroy.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_schema_get_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_schema_get_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_schema_handle</span> <span class="nv">schema</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_schema_get_field"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_schema_get_field</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_schema_handle</span> <span class="nv">schema</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_schema_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_schema_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_schema_handle</span> *<span class="nv">schema</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_schema_get_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of fields in a schema.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_schema_get_count(
  duckdb_v2_schema_handle schema,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `schema`: The schema.
* `out_count`: Receives the field count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_schema_get_field`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the name and type of the field at the given index.

out_name and out_type are valid only until the schema is destroyed, and
out_type must not be destroyed. An out-of-range index is rejected with
ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_schema_get_field(
  duckdb_v2_schema_handle schema,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *out_name,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `schema`: The schema.
* `index`: Zero-based field index.
* `out_name`: Receives a borrowed view of the field name. Valid until the schema is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `out_type`: Receives a borrowed field type. Valid until the schema is destroyed; do not destroy it. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_schema_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a schema handle.

Frees the handle along with the names and types it owns. On success the
slot is set to null. Safe to call on an already-null slot.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_schema_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_schema_handle *schema
);
```

##### Parameters

* `schema`: The schema handle to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Tokenizer

#### `duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to an iterator over the tokens of a SQL string, produced by tokenize_sql.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE`

The lexical class of a token.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_INVALID` = 0: Not an actual token class; out_type is set to this when [`duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next`](#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next) fails.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_KEYWORD` = 1: A keyword of the connection's grammar.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_IDENTIFIER` = 2: A bare or double-quoted identifier, quotes included.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_STRING_LITERAL` = 3: A quoted or dollar-quoted string, delimiters included.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_NUMBER_LITERAL` = 4: A numeric literal.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_OPERATOR` = 5: An operator or punctuation run other than the statement terminator.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_COMMENT` = 6: A line or block comment, delimiters included.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_TERMINATOR` = 7: A statement-terminating semicolon.
* `DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE_END_OF_INPUT` = 8: Not a token; reported by token_iterator_next once the input is exhausted, with start equal to the input length and length 0.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_tokenize_sql"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_tokenize_sql</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">sql</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_iterator</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle</span> <span class="nv">iterator</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE</span> *<span class="nv">out_type</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_start</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">out_length</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle</span> <span class="nv">iterator</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> *<span class="nv">out_ends_unterminated</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle</span> *<span class="nv">iterator</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_tokenize_sql`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Tokenizes a SQL string into an iterator over its tokens.

Lexical tokenization, in the context of whatever grammar extensions are loaded on the given connection. Closing
the connection or changing settings afterwards does not affect the tokens. The SQL string is borrowed for the call
only, the caller may free it once this call returns. Whitespace is not a token. Malformed input is not an error;
[`duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated`](#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated) reports whether the input ended inside an open token.

*out_iterator is set to NULL on failure.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_tokenize_sql(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  const duckdb_v2_str *sql,
  duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle *out_iterator,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection supplying the grammar.
* `sql`: The SQL text. Borrowed for the call only; may contain interior null bytes. {NULL, 0} is the empty input.
* `out_iterator`: Receives the new iterator handle. Destroy via token_iterator_destroy. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Yields the next token, or END_OF_INPUT once exhausted.

On success writes the token's class, byte offset and byte length into the out-parameters. The lexeme is the input
bytes [start, start + length). Once the input is exhausted, every call gives TOKEN_TYPE_END_OF_INPUT with start
equal to the input length and length 0. On failure out params are set to TOKEN_TYPE_INVALID, 0, 0.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next(
  duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle iterator,
  DUCKDB_V2_TOKEN_TYPE *out_type,
  idx_t *out_start,
  idx_t *out_length,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `iterator`: The iterator to advance.
* `out_type`: Receives the token's class, or TOKEN_TYPE_END_OF_INPUT once exhausted. (out)
* `out_start`: Receives the token's byte offset into the input; the input length for END_OF_INPUT. (out)
* `out_length`: Receives the token's byte length; 0 for END_OF_INPUT. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Reports whether the input ended before the closing delimiter of its last token.

True when the input ends inside an open string, quoted identifier, block comment or dollar-quoted string, or in a
line comment with no trailing newline; false otherwise, including for empty or whitespace-only input.
Equivalently, the last token [`duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next`](#duckdb_v2_token_iterator_next) yields before TOKEN_TYPE_END_OF_INPUT is the open one, so
its class and lexeme say which delimiter is missing. A property of the input, not of the iterator position: the
answer is the same before, during and after draining. The only failure is a null argument.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_token_iterator_ends_unterminated(
  duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle iterator,
  bool *out_ends_unterminated,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `iterator`: The iterator.
* `out_ends_unterminated`: Receives whether the input ended inside an open token. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_token_iterator_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a token iterator handle.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_token_iterator_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_token_iterator_handle *iterator
);
```

##### Parameters

* `iterator`: The iterator to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Aggregate

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom aggregate function being built. Created with
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_create), configured with
the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback), etc.)
and the signature obtained via [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature), made available with
[`duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the result of an aggregate function's “bind” phase. The “bind” callback receives
this handle next to a [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle), which gives access to the arguments, the user data and the
bind data, and can use it to set the return type of the call site being bound.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the state sizing “size”
phase. The “size” callback receives this handle and must use it to report the size of a single aggregate
state in bytes.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_init_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the state
initialization “init” phase. The “init” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the array
of aggregate states it must initialize in place.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_update_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the “update” phase.
The “update” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the input argument vectors, the
number of rows to process, and the aggregate state each row must be aggregated into.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_combine_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the “combine” phase.
The “combine” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the source and target aggregate
state arrays to merge.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_finalize_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the “finalize” phase.
The “finalize” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the aggregate states and the result
vector and offset to write their final values to.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to an aggregate function during the state destruction
“destroy” phase. The “destroy” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the array of
aggregate states whose resources must be released.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_info_handle result,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the arguments of the call site being bound, the user data and
the bind data.
* `result`: Borrowed opaque handle to set the return type of the call site being bound through.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

<br>

##### Syntax

```c

);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback. Errors reported by this callback are ignored.

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new aggregate function through a factory.

The function starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name),
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback), etc.) and the signature obtained via
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature), then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function). The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy), also after registration.

The aggregate function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the aggregate function through.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created aggregate function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the aggregate function.

The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name.
A name must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_docs`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the documentation of the function so it can be filled in.

Set a description with [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description), and add examples and categories with
[`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example) and [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category). The documentation is modified in place, describes this overload only, and is
registered with the function. Optional.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_docs(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle *docs,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to get the documentation of.
* `docs`: The returned documentation. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the function's signature so it can be configured.

Add parameters with [`duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter`](#duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter) and set the return type with
[`duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type`](#duckdb_v2_function_signature_set_return_type).
The signature is modified in place; the function must be given a signature with a return type before
registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_get_signature(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle *sig,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to get the signature of.
* `sig`: The returned signature. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the aggregate function.

Associates an opaque pointer with the function, retrievable from each callback via its user data accessor
(e.g. [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data), [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_update_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_update_get_user_data), etc.).
The opaque handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor, invoked when the data is no longer
needed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_property`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets a property on the aggregate function.

Configures a function property that influences planning and execution, such as stability, NULL handling,
fallibility, collation handling, or the aggregate-specific order/DISTINCT dependence. The value must be
one of the [`DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_VALUE`](#duckdb_v2_function_property_value) entries belonging to `key`; passing a value that does not belong
to the key, or a key that is not valid for aggregate functions, results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_property(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_KEY key,
  DUCKDB_V2_FUNCTION_PROPERTY_VALUE value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the property of.
* `key`: The property to set.
* `value`: The value to set for the property. Must belong to `key`.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_bind_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional bind callback of the aggregate function.

The bind callback is invoked during query planning for each call site of the function. Through its
[`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle) it can inspect the argument types and constant argument values and set “bind data”
that is shared with the other callbacks. Through its [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_info_handle) it can set a concrete
return type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_bind_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the bind callback of.
* `callback`: The bind callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_size_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the size callback of the aggregate function.

The size callback reports the size of a single aggregate state in bytes via
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_set_state_size`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_set_state_size); DuckDB uses it to allocate state memory.
A size callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_size_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the size callback of.
* `callback`: The size callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_init_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the init callback of the aggregate function.

The init callback initializes freshly allocated aggregate states in place, obtained via
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_init_get_states`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_init_get_states). An init callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_init_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_init_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the init callback of.
* `callback`: The init callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the update callback of the aggregate function.

The update callback is invoked during query execution with a batch of input rows: row i of every argument
vector must be aggregated into state i of the state array. An update callback must be set before
registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_update_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_update_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the update callback of.
* `callback`: The update callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_combine_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the combine callback of the aggregate function.

The combine callback merges partial aggregate states computed in parallel: source state i must be
combined into target state i. A combine callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_combine_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_combine_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the combine callback of.
* `callback`: The combine callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_finalize_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the finalize callback of the aggregate function.

The finalize callback produces the function's result: state i must be finalized into result row
offset + i of the result vector. A finalize callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_finalize_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_finalize_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the finalize callback of.
* `callback`: The finalize callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_destroy_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the destroy callback for the aggregate function. Optional: only
needed when aggregate states own resources that must be released. The
callback runs on states that are discarded without being finalized; it
must not fail, an error reported through its error slot is ignored.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_destroy_callback(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the destroy callback of.
* `callback`: The destroy callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_set_return_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the concrete return type of the call site being bound.

Overrides the return type declared in the signature. Register the function with an ANY return type and set
the concrete type here, derived from the argument types, to build a function whose result type depends on
its input. The type is borrowed and copied.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_set_return_type(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle return_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `return_type`: The return type to set. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_get_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the user data set via [`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_set_user_data).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_get_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The size info handle.
* `data`: Receives the user data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_get_bind_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the bind data set by the function's bind callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_get_bind_data(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The size info handle.
* `data`: Receives the bind data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_size_set_state_size`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the size of a single aggregate state, in bytes. The size callback
must set this; DuckDB uses it to allocate state memory.

##### Syntax


#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the aggregate function, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The function is registered on the connection's database, visible to every connection, in the connection's
transaction: inside an explicit transaction, it is invisible to other connections until the transaction commits,
and a rollback undoes it. Registration requires a name, the size, init, update, combine and finalize callbacks,
and a signature with a complete return type; an ANY return type is accepted only together with a bind callback
that sets the concrete type per call site. The aggregate function must have been created through a factory of the
same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_aggregate_function(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `function`: The aggregate function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the aggregate function, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The function is registered on the loading extension's database and attributed to the extension. Use this from the
extension's load callback. Registration requires a name, the size, init, update, combine and finalize callbacks,
and a signature with a complete return type; an ANY return type is accepted only together with a bind callback
that sets the concrete type per call site. The aggregate function must have been created through a factory of the
same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_aggregate_function(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `function`: The aggregate function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the aggregate function, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered
function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_aggregate_function_handle *function
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Catalog

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_handle`

An owned snapshot of one base table taken at creation: where the name resolved, the table's columns, and
per-column catalog facts. Later DDL does not update it. Create with [`duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table`](#duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table), read the
resolved location via [`duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname), and the columns via
[`duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count) and [`duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column). Destroy via
[`duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_handle`

An owned snapshot of one column of a described table: its name, type, and catalog facts. Obtain with
[`duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column), read with [`duckdb_v2_column_description_get_name`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_get_name),
[`duckdb_v2_column_description_get_type`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_get_type), [`duckdb_v2_column_description_has_default`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_has_default) and
[`duckdb_v2_column_description_has_generated`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_has_generated), and destroy with [`duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy).

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_connection_handle</span> <span class="nv">conn</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> <span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_table_description_handle</span> *<span class="nv">desc</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_table_description_handle</span> <span class="nv">desc</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_qname_handle</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_table_description_is_readonly"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_table_description_is_readonly</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_table_description_handle</span> <span class="nv">desc</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> *<span class="nv">readonly</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_table_description_handle</span> <span class="nv">desc</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_table_description_handle</span> <span class="nv">desc</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_column_description_handle</span> *<span class="nv">column</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Resolves a table name and snapshots its description.

Resolves name in the connection's catalogs and returns an owned description of the table it names. name may be
partial: an unqualified or schema-qualified name resolves through the connection's search path, exactly as the
same name resolves in SQL. A two-part name tries the first part as a schema and as an attached database, as SQL
does, and is rejected when both readings exist. A name that resolves to nothing is rejected with the engine's
missing-table error; a name that resolves to a view is rejected with the engine's not-a-table error, since a
description snapshots a base table.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_describe_table(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle *desc,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection whose catalogs and search path resolve the name.
* `name`: The possibly partial table name to resolve. Borrowed for the call only.
* `desc`: On success, receives the owned description. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the resolved qualified name of the described table.

Returns an owned copy of the fully resolved name: the catalog, schema, and table the lookup landed on, with the
casing the table was created with, never an echo of the requested name. Rendering it produces SQL that pins the
described table regardless of search path.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_table_description_get_qname(
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle desc,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `desc`: The description.
* `name`: Receives the owned resolved name. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_is_readonly`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns whether the described table's catalog is read-only.

True when the catalog the name resolved into was attached read-only, in which case no write to the table can
succeed. False does not by itself prove a write will succeed; it clears the catalog-level check only.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_table_description_is_readonly(
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle desc,
  bool *readonly,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `desc`: The description.
* `readonly`: Receives whether the catalog is read-only. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of columns of the described table.

Counts every column in declared order, generated columns included. Valid indices for
[`duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column`](#duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column) are [0, count).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column_count(
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle desc,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `desc`: The description.
* `count`: Receives the column count. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns an owned description of the column at index.

Columns are numbered in declared order, generated columns included. An out-of-range index is rejected with
`ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_table_description_get_column(
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle desc,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_column_description_handle *column,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `desc`: The description.
* `index`: Zero-based column index.
* `column`: Receives the owned column description. Destroy via [`duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the table description, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Column descriptions obtained from it are independent and stay valid.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_table_description_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_table_description_handle *desc
);
```

##### Parameters

* `desc`: The description to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_get_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the name of the column.

The name carries the casing the column was declared with.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_description_get_name(

);
```

##### Parameters

* `column`: The column description.
* `name`: Receives a borrowed view of the column name. Valid until the column description is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_get_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the type of the column.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_description_get_type(
```

##### Parameters

* `column`: The column description.
* `type`: Receives the borrowed column type. Valid until the column description is destroyed; do not destroy it. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_has_default`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns whether the column has a default value.

True when the column declares a default expression; the engine evaluates it for rows that omit the column.
Generated columns report false.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_description_has_default(
  duckdb_v2_column_description_handle column,
  bool *has_default,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err

```

##### Parameters

* `column`: The column description.
* `has_default`: Receives whether the column has a default value. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_has_generated`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns whether the column is generated.

True when the column is a generated column, computed by the engine from a generation expression and not
writable.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_description_has_generated(
  duckdb_v2_column_description_handle column,
  bool *has_generated,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err

```

##### Parameters

* `column`: The column description.
* `has_generated`: Receives whether the column is generated. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the column description, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Any name or type borrowed from it becomes dangling.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_column_description_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_column_description_handle *column
);
```

##### Parameters

* `column`: The column description to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

### Copy

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom copy function being built: an output format for `COPY ... TO`, an input
format for `COPY ... FROM`, or both. Created with [`duckdb_v2_copy_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_create), configured with the setter functions (e.g.
[`duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_callback`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_callback), [`duckdb_v2_copy_from_set_exec_callback`](#duckdb_v2_copy_from_set_exec_callback), etc.), made
available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_copy_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_copy_function), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the query preparation “bind” phase
of a `COPY ... TO` statement. The “bind” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. inspect the names
and types of the columns being written, read the statement's options and initialize some constant state.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_size_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the “batch size” phase of a
`COPY ... TO` statement. The “batch size” callback receives this handle and must use it to report how many rows
a batch should carry.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_init_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the per-file “init” phase of a
`COPY ... TO` statement. The “init” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. read the path of the
file being written and set up the state shared by every batch written to that file.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the “batch” phase of a
`COPY ... TO` statement. The “batch” callback receives this handle and can use it to take ownership of the rows
of the batch and to set the prepared form of the batch handed to the “flush” callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_flush_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the “flush” phase of a
`COPY ... TO` statement. The “flush” callback receives this handle and can use it to access the prepared batch
and write it to the output.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_finalize_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the per-file “finalize” phase of a
`COPY ... TO` statement. The “finalize” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. close the file
after every batch has been flushed to it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_statistics_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function when a `COPY ... TO` statement reports
statistics about the files it wrote (e.g. with `RETURN_STATS`). The “statistics” callback receives this
handle and uses it to report the statistics of one written file.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_bind_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the query preparation “bind” phase
of a `COPY ... FROM` statement. The “bind” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. read the path of
the file to read, inspect the names and types of the columns the target table expects, read the statement's
options, hint at the number of rows the read will produce and initialize some constant state.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_init_global_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the global state initialization
“init global” phase of a `COPY ... FROM` statement. The “init global” callback receives this handle and can use
it to e.g. set up the state shared by every thread reading the file, and to declare how many threads may read
it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_init_local_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the local state initialization
“init local” phase of a `COPY ... FROM` statement. The “init local” callback receives this handle and can use it
to e.g. set up worker-local state, typically by claiming work from the shared global state.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the execution “exec” phase of a
`COPY ... FROM` statement. The “exec” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. access the global and
local state and write the next batch of rows to the output chunk.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_progress_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a copy function during the “progress” phase of a
`COPY ... FROM` statement. The “progress” callback receives this handle and can use it to report how far the read
has advanced.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new copy function through a factory.

A copy function implements a file format for `COPY`: once registered, SQL reaches it with `COPY ... TO 'path'
(FORMAT name)` and `COPY table FROM 'path' (FORMAT name)`. The function starts out empty: configure it with the
setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name), the `copy_to_set_*` callbacks for writing, the
`copy_from_set_*` callbacks for reading, or both), then make it available with
[`duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_copy_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_copy_function). The caller owns the returned
handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy), also after registration.

The copy function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the copy function through.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created copy function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the copy function.

The name is the format SQL selects the function with: `COPY ... TO 'path' (FORMAT name)` or
`COPY table FROM 'path' (FORMAT name)`. It is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous
name. A name must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_file_extension`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the file extension of the files the copy function writes, without the leading dot, e.g. `parquet`.

DuckDB uses it when it names files itself, e.g. the files of `COPY ... TO 'dir' (PARTITION_BY ...)` or
`(PER_THREAD_OUTPUT)`. A statement can override it with the `FILE_EXTENSION` option. An extension starting with
a dot is rejected. The extension is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous extension.
Optional, but without it the names DuckDB gives files end in a bare dot, e.g. `data_0.`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_file_extension(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_str *extension,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the file extension of.
* `extension`: The extension to set, without the leading dot. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the copy function.

Associates an opaque pointer with the function, retrievable from each callback of either side via its user data
accessor (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_get_user_data), [`duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_get_user_data), etc.). The opaque handle
bundles the pointer with an optional destructor, invoked when the data is no longer needed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_function_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_bind_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional bind callback of the `COPY ... TO` side.

The bind callback is invoked during query planning for each `COPY ... TO` statement that uses the function. It
can inspect the names and types of the columns being written, read the statement's options and set “bind data”
that is shared with the other `COPY ... TO` callbacks.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_bind_callback(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the callback of.
* `callback`: The callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_size_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional batch size callback of the `COPY ... TO` side.

The batch size callback is invoked during query planning, after the bind callback, for each `COPY ... TO`
statement that does not set `BATCH_SIZE` itself. It should report how many rows a batch should carry via
[`duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_size_set_target`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_size_set_target); the engine then cuts the rows being written into batches of that size and
hands each to the batch callback. Without a batch size from either the statement or the callback, a batch is
cut for every chunk of rows sunk, i.e. a vector at a time. A batch may still be smaller than the reported size
(the last one of a file, or when `BATCH_SIZE_BYTES` cuts it first).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_size_callback(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_size_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the callback of.
* `callback`: The callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_init_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional init callback of the `COPY ... TO` side.

The init callback is invoked once per output file, before any batch destined for that file is prepared. It can
read the path of the file via [`duckdb_v2_copy_to_init_get_file_path`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_init_get_file_path) and set “init data” that is shared with the
batch, flush and finalize callbacks of that file. A statement may write several files, e.g. when its output is
partitioned; each gets its own init data.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_init_callback(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_copy_to_init_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the callback of.
* `callback`: The callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the batch callback of the `COPY ... TO` side.

The batch callback is invoked during query execution with a batch of the rows being written, taken via
[`duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_take_input`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_take_input). It prepares the batch for writing, e.g. by encoding it into the output format,
and sets “batch data” via [`duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_set_batch_data`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_set_batch_data) that is handed to the flush callback. Batches may
be prepared by several threads at once, so the callback must synchronize its own access to the init data. A
batch callback must be set for the `COPY ... TO` side to be registered.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_batch_callback(
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the callback of.
* `callback`: The callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_get_option_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the value of the option at the given index.

An option written with a single value (e.g. `DELIM ','`) yields that value. An option written as a bare name
(e.g. `HEADER`) yields the BOOLEAN `true`. An option written with a parenthesized list (e.g. `KEYS (a, b)`)
yields a tuple: an unnamed STRUCT with one field per element, in order. Fails if the index is out of bounds.
The returned value is owned by the caller and must be destroyed via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c

  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The bind info handle.
* `index`: The index of the option.
* `value`: Receives the option's value. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_take_input`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Takes ownership of the rows of the batch to prepare.

The collection holds one column per column reported by [`duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_get_column_count`](#duckdb_v2_copy_to_bind_get_column_count), in the same order,
and can be scanned with [`duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_scan`](#duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_scan). The batch can only be taken once: a second call
fails. Once taken, the caller owns the collection and must destroy it via [`duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_destroy),
e.g. by keeping it as the batch data with that destructor. A batch that is never taken is destroyed when the
callback returns.

##### Syntax

```c

  duckdb_v2_copy_to_batch_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle *collection,
```

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_set_bind_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the bind callback of the `COPY ... FROM` side.

The bind callback is invoked during query planning for each `COPY ... FROM` statement that uses the function.
It can read the path of the file to read and the statement's options, inspect the names and types of the
columns the target table expects, hint at the number of rows the read will produce, and set “bind data” that is
shared with the other `COPY ... FROM` callbacks. The columns are fixed by the target table: the function must
produce them as they are. A bind callback must be set for the `COPY ... FROM` side to be registered.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_get_output_chunk`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the output chunk the exec callback must write the next batch of rows into.

The chunk holds one vector per column reported by [`duckdb_v2_copy_from_bind_get_column_count`](#duckdb_v2_copy_from_bind_get_column_count), in the same order;
reach them with [`duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector`](#duckdb_v2_data_chunk_get_vector). The chunk starts out empty on every invocation: write the rows,
then declare how many there are with [`duckdb_v2_vector_set_size`](#duckdb_v2_vector_set_size) on the first vector, which the engine takes as the
batch's row count and propagates to the other vectors. Producing an empty batch signals the end of the read,
after which the callback is not invoked again on that thread. Borrowed; valid only for the duration of the
callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_get_output_chunk(
  duckdb_v2_copy_from_exec_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_data_chunk_handle *chunk,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `chunk`: Receives the borrowed output chunk to write into. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the copy function, making it available as a `COPY` format.

The function is registered on the connection's database, visible to every connection, in the connection's
transaction: inside an explicit transaction, it is invisible to other connections until the transaction commits,
and a rollback undoes it. Registration requires a name and at least one configured side: a `COPY ... TO` side
needs its batch and flush callbacks, a `COPY ... FROM` side needs its bind and exec callbacks. A statement in a
direction the function does not implement fails with an error. The copy function must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_copy_function(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_copy_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `function`: The copy function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

needs its batch and flush callbacks, a `COPY ... FROM` side needs its bind and exec callbacks. A statement in a
direction the function does not implement fails with an error. The copy function must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_copy_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_copy_to_set_statistics_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional statistics callback of the `COPY ... TO` side.

The statistics callback reports statistics about a written file, such as the number of rows and bytes it
holds, which `COPY ... TO` returns when the statement asks for them with `RETURN_STATS`. It is invoked once
per output file, after the finalize callback of that file, and only when the statement asks for the
statistics. Without a statistics callback, `RETURN_STATS` is rejected for the function.

### Custom Option

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom option being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_create`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_create), configured with
the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_type`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_type), etc.), made available
with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option), and destroyed with
[`duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to an update of a custom option, received by its update callback. It gives access to
the new value, the scope it is written at and the user data, and can replace the value.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the update and the user data.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context setting the option. When the option is written through the config of an
instance, or given at startup, this is an internal context rather than a user's connection: its session
state is discarded after the update.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback. Reporting an error
refuses the update: the option keeps its previous value.

<br>

<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle</span> <span class="nv">option</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
