#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new custom option through a factory.

The option starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions, then make it available with
[`duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option). The caller owns the returned
handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy), also after registration.

The custom option can only be registered on the instance the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle *option,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the custom option through.
* `option`: On success, receives the newly created custom option. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the custom option, as `SET` and the config functions refer to it.

The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name. A name must be set before
registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the type of the custom option. Every value written to the option is cast to it, as SQL `SET` does.

The type is borrowed and copied. Optional when a default value is set, whose type the option then takes.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_type(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the type of.
* `type`: The type to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_default_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the default value of the custom option: its value until it is set, and the value `RESET` restores.

The value is borrowed and copied, and cast to the option's type at registration, which fails when the cast
does. Without a default value the option reads as NULL until it is set.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_default_value(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the default value of.
* `value`: The default value. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_description`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the description of the custom option, as [`duckdb_v2_option_get_description`](#duckdb_v2_option_get_description) and `duckdb_settings()` report it.

The description is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous description.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_description(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  const duckdb_v2_str *description,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the description of.
* `description`: The description to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_default_scope`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the scope a write at `SETTING_SCOPE_DEFAULT` goes to, like SQL `SET name = value`.

Must be GLOBAL or SESSION, and a scope the option supports. Defaults to SESSION, or to GLOBAL when the option
does not support SESSION.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_default_scope(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE scope,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the default scope of.
* `scope`: The default scope, GLOBAL or SESSION.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_supports_scope`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets whether the custom option can be written at a scope, as [`duckdb_v2_option_supports_scope`](#duckdb_v2_option_supports_scope) reports it.

A custom option supports both GLOBAL and SESSION unless told otherwise. A write at a scope it does not support
fails, from SQL as from [`duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value`](#duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value). Registration fails when the option supports neither scope.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_supports_scope(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  DUCKDB_V2_SETTING_SCOPE scope,
  bool supported,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to configure.
* `scope`: The scope, GLOBAL or SESSION.
* `supported`: Whether the option can be written at the scope.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the custom option.

Associates an opaque pointer with the option, retrievable from the update callback via
[`duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_user_data). The opaque handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor,
invoked when the data is no longer needed: once the custom option handle is destroyed and, if it was
registered, the instance is too.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_update_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional update callback of the custom option.

The callback is invoked whenever the option is set or reset, from SQL as from [`duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value`](#duckdb_v2_config_set_option_value), after the
new value is cast to the option's type and before it is stored. It may replace the value with
[`duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_set_value`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_set_value), or refuse it by reporting an error. It is not invoked for the default value
at registration, nor for a value given to the instance at startup. The callback must not write options itself.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_update_callback(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to set the update callback of.
* `callback`: The update callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the user data set via [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_set_user_data).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The update info handle.
* `data`: Receives the user data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the value the option is updated to, already cast to the option's type. On a reset this is the
default value, which may be NULL. The returned value is owned by the caller and must be destroyed via
[`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_value(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The update info handle.
* `value`: Receives the new value. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_set_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Replaces the value the option is updated to, e.g. to normalize it. The value is borrowed and copied, and cast to
the option's type, which fails when the cast does.

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_set_value(
```

##### Parameters

* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the scope the value is written at: GLOBAL or SESSION, a DEFAULT write already resolved to the option's

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_update_get_scope(
```

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the custom option on the connection's instance, visible to every connection.

Registration is not transactional: it takes effect at once, also inside an explicit transaction, and a rollback
does not undo it. Registration requires a name and a type, or a default value to take the type from, and fails
when an option of the same name already exists. A value given for the option at startup is picked up. The custom
option must have been created through a factory of the same instance. The caller still owns the handle after
registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy), which does not affect the registered option.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_custom_option(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `option`: The custom option to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the custom option on the loading extension's instance, visible to every connection.

Use this from the extension's load callback. Registration is not transactional, requires a name and a type, or a
default value to take the type from, and fails when an option of the same name already exists. A value given
for the option at startup is picked up. The custom option must have been created through a factory of the same
instance. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy), which does not affect the registered option.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_custom_option(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle option,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `option`: The custom option to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the custom option, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered option.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_custom_option_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_custom_option_handle *option
);
```

##### Parameters

* `option`: The option to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Expression

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to a node of a bound expression tree. Read-only and owned by the engine: valid only
for the duration of the callback that handed it out, and never destroyed by the caller. Child nodes borrowed
via [`duckdb_v2_expression_get_child`](#duckdb_v2_expression_get_child) share their parent's lifetime.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE`

The type of a bound expression node. The values mirror the engine's own expression types, restricted to the
node types a filter predicate can contain; every other node type is reported as `EXPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID`.

Comparisons, `BETWEEN` and casts are regular scalar function calls once bound: they have the function's
children and name, and only their type tells them apart from any other function. A `CAST` therefore has one
child, the value being cast, and its target type is the node's return type.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID` = 0: A node type this API does not model. Its children can still be walked.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_CAST` = 12: A cast. One child; the target type is the node's return type and [`duckdb_v2_expression_cast_get_mode`](#duckdb_v2_expression_cast_get_mode) tells a `TRY_CAST` apart.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_NOT` = 13: Logical `NOT`. One child.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_IS_NULL` = 14: `IS NULL`. One child.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_IS_NOT_NULL` = 15: `IS NOT NULL`. One child.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_EQUAL` = 25: `=`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_NOTEQUAL` = 26: `<>`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_LESSTHAN` = 27: `<`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_GREATERTHAN` = 28: `>`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_LESSTHANOREQUALTO` = 29: `<=`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_GREATERTHANOREQUALTO` = 30: `>=`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_IN` = 35: `IN`. The first child is the value tested, the remaining children are the candidates.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_NOT_IN` = 36: `NOT IN`. The first child is the value tested, the remaining children are the candidates.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_DISTINCT_FROM` = 37: `IS DISTINCT FROM`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_BETWEEN` = 38: `BETWEEN`. Three children: the value tested, the lower bound and the upper bound.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_NOT_DISTINCT_FROM` = 40: `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`. Two children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_CONJUNCTION_AND` = 50: Logical `AND`. Two or more children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_CONJUNCTION_OR` = 51: Logical `OR`. Two or more children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_VALUE_CONSTANT` = 75: A constant. No children; read it with [`duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value`](#duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value).
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_VALUE_PARAMETER` = 76: A prepared statement parameter whose value is not known yet. No children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_BOUND_FUNCTION` = 141: A call to a scalar function other than the ones listed above. The children are its arguments; read the name with [`duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name`](#duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name).
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_CASE_EXPR` = 150: A `CASE` expression. The children are each `WHEN` condition followed by its `THEN` result, then the `ELSE` result.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_COALESCE` = 152: `COALESCE`. One or more children.
* `DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE_BOUND_COLUMN_REF` = 228: A reference to a column. No children; read it with [`duckdb_v2_expression_column_ref_get_index`](#duckdb_v2_expression_column_ref_get_index).

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_expression_get_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_expression_get_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> <span class="nv">expression</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE</span> *<span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_expression_get_return_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_expression_get_return_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> <span class="nv">expression</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_expression_get_child_count"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_expression_get_child_count</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> <span class="nv">expression</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_expression_get_child"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_expression_get_child</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> <span class="nv">expression</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">index</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> *<span class="nv">child</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_expression_handle</span> <span class="nv">expression</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_value_handle</span> *<span class="nv">value</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_get_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the type of an expression node.

The type decides which of the type-specific accessors apply, and what the node's children mean; see
`EXPRESSION_TYPE`. A node of a type this API does not model reports `EXPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID`.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_get_type(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  DUCKDB_V2_EXPRESSION_TYPE *type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The expression node.
* `type`: Receives the node type. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_get_return_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the logical type the expression node evaluates to.

For a cast this is the target type. The returned type is owned by the caller and must be destroyed via
[`duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_get_return_type(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The expression node.
* `type`: Receives the owned logical type. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_get_child_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of child nodes of an expression node.

Works for every node type, including `EXPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID`. Constants, parameters and column references
have no children.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_get_child_count(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  idx_t *count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The expression node.
* `count`: Receives the number of children. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_get_child`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves a child node of an expression node by index.

Fails if the index is out of bounds. Children are ordered as the node type describes (see
`EXPRESSION_TYPE`). The child is borrowed and shares the lifetime of its parent.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_get_child(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle *child,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The expression node.
* `index`: The index of the child to retrieve.
* `child`: Receives the borrowed child node. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the value of a constant node.

Fails if the node is not of type `EXPRESSION_TYPE_VALUE_CONSTANT`. The returned value is owned by the caller
and must be destroyed via [`duckdb_v2_value_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_value_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_constant_get_value(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The constant node.
* `value`: Receives the owned constant value. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_column_ref_get_index`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the column a column reference node points at.

Fails if the node is not of type `EXPRESSION_TYPE_BOUND_COLUMN_REF`. The index counts the columns of the
operator the predicate is evaluated against, which is not necessarily the full set of columns that operator
can produce: a callback resolves it through whatever handed it the expression, e.g.
[`duckdb_v2_table_function_filter_pushdown_get_column_index`](#duckdb_v2_table_function_filter_pushdown_get_column_index) for a filter offered to a table function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_column_ref_get_index(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  idx_t *index,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The column reference node.
* `index`: Receives the column index. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the name of the scalar function a function node calls.

Applies to `EXPRESSION_TYPE_BOUND_FUNCTION` and to the node types that are function calls underneath: the
comparisons, `EXPRESSION_TYPE_COMPARE_BETWEEN` and `EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_CAST`. Fails for any other node
type. For a comparison the name is its operator, e.g. `<`; for `BETWEEN` and casts it is an internal name, so
dispatch on the type rather than the name for those. The name is borrowed and shares the lifetime of the node.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The function node.
* `name`: Receives a borrowed view of the function name. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_qname`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the qualified name of the scalar function a function node calls.

Applies to the same node types as [`duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name`](#duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_name), and fails for any other. The name is
qualified with the catalog and schema the function was resolved in, where known. The returned name is owned
by the caller and must be destroyed via [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_function_get_qname(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The function node.
* `name`: Receives the owned qualified name. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_expression_cast_get_mode`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns whether a cast node is a regular `CAST` or a `TRY_CAST`.

Fails if the node is not of type `EXPRESSION_TYPE_OPERATOR_CAST`. A `TRY_CAST` yields NULL for a value it
cannot convert where a regular `CAST` would fail the query.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_expression_cast_get_mode(
  duckdb_v2_expression_handle expression,
  DUCKDB_V2_CAST_MODE *mode,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `expression`: The cast node.
* `mode`: Receives the cast mode. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Log Sink

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a log sink being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_create`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_create), configured with
[`duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_write_callback`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_write_callback) and the other setters, made available with
[`duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink`](#duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink), and destroyed with
[`duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the context of a log entry, received by a log sink's write callback next to the
entry itself, and valid only for the duration of that call. Read the ids `duckdb_logs` reports for the entry
through its getters, e.g. [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_connection_id`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_connection_id).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_flush_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle received by a log sink's flush callback, and valid only for the duration of that call.
It carries nothing yet.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle info,
  void *user_data,
  int64_t timestamp,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOG_LEVEL level,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOG_SCOPE scope,
  const duckdb_v2_str *type,
  const duckdb_v2_str *message,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle to the context of the entry, giving access to its ids.
* `user_data`: The user data set via [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data), or null if none was set.
* `timestamp`: When the entry was written, as a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE - microseconds since the epoch.
* `level`: The severity of the entry.
* `scope`: The scope the entry was written in, which decides which of its ids are present.
* `type`: The log type the entry was written under, e.g. `QueryLog`. Borrowed for the duration of the call.
* `message`: The message of the entry. Borrowed for the duration of the call.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to report a failure to receive the entry through. A reported error drops the
entry; it never fails the operation that logged.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_flush_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_log_sink_flush_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_flush_info_handle info,
  void *user_data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle to the flush. Carries nothing yet.
* `user_data`: The user data set via [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data), or null if none was set.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to report a failure to flush through. A reported error is dropped; it never
fails the operation that flushed.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_SCOPE`

The scope a log entry was written in, which decides which of its ids are present.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_SCOPE_DATABASE` = 10: Written for the database as a whole, carrying no connection, transaction or query id.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_SCOPE_CONNECTION` = 20: Written by a connection, carrying its connection id and, inside one, the transaction and query ids.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOG_SCOPE_THREAD` = 30: Written by a thread executing a query, carrying the thread id next to the connection's ids.

<br>

<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_thread_id"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_thread_id</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle</span> <span class="nv">info</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> *<span class="nv">id</span>, <span class="kt">bool</span> *<span class="nv">present</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_instance_handle</span> <span class="nv">instance</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle</span> <span class="nv">sink</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_extension_handle</span> <span class="nv">extension</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle</span> <span class="nv">sink</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle</span> *<span class="nv">sink</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new log sink through a factory.

The log sink starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions, then make it available with
[`duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink`](#duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink). The caller owns the returned handle and
must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy), also after registration.

The log sink can only be registered on the instance the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle *sink,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the log sink through.
* `sink`: On success, receives the newly created log sink. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name the logging configuration refers to the log sink by.

Names are matched case-insensitively. The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous
name. A name must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sink`: The log sink to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the log sink.

Associates an opaque pointer with the sink, handed to its write and flush callbacks. The opaque handle bundles
the pointer with an optional destructor, invoked when the data is no longer needed: when the instance is
destroyed if the sink was registered, else when the log sink handle is.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sink`: The log sink to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_write_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the write callback of the log sink, invoked for every entry the logging configuration directs to the sink.

The callback must return quickly, must be safe to run concurrently and on any thread, and must not log or change
the logging configuration. A write callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_write_callback(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sink`: The log sink to set the write callback of.
* `callback`: The write callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_flush_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional flush callback of the log sink, invoked when DuckDB flushes its log, so entries the sink holds
on to can be written out. When DuckDB flushes is up to DuckDB; entries still held when the instance is destroyed
are for the user data's destructor to write out.

Like the write callback, it must be safe to run on any thread, and must not log or change the logging
configuration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_set_flush_callback(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_flush_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sink`: The log sink to set the flush callback of.
* `callback`: The flush callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_connection_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the id of the connection that wrote the entry, as `duckdb_logs` reports it. An entry written for the
database as a whole has none: `present` then receives false and `id` is left untouched.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_connection_id(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle info,
  idx_t *id,
  bool *present,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The write info handle of the entry.
* `id`: Receives the connection id, if present. (out)
* `present`: Receives whether the entry has a connection id. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_transaction_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the id of the transaction the entry was written in, as `duckdb_logs` reports it. An entry written
outside a transaction has none: `present` then receives false and `id` is left untouched.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_transaction_id(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle info,
  idx_t *id,
  bool *present,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The write info handle of the entry.
* `id`: Receives the transaction id, if present. (out)
* `present`: Receives whether the entry has a transaction id. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_query_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the id of the query the entry was written for, as `duckdb_logs` reports it. An entry written outside
a query has none: `present` then receives false and `id` is left untouched.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_query_id(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle info,
  idx_t *id,
  bool *present,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The write info handle of the entry.
* `id`: Receives the query id, if present. (out)
* `present`: Receives whether the entry has a query id. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_thread_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the id of the thread that wrote the entry, as `duckdb_logs` reports it. Only an entry written in the
thread scope has one: otherwise `present` receives false and `id` is left untouched. The id identifies the
thread that logged, which need not be the thread the write callback runs on.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_get_thread_id(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_write_info_handle info,
  idx_t *id,
  bool *present,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The write info handle of the entry.
* `id`: Receives the thread id, if present. (out)
* `present`: Receives whether the entry has a thread id. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the log sink on the instance, making it available to the logging configuration under its name.

Registering does not direct any entries to the sink by itself; the logging configuration does. Registration is
not transactional, requires a name and a write callback, and fails when the name is taken: by a sink DuckDB
provides itself, such as `memory`, `stdout` or `file`, or by a sink registered before. The log sink must have
been created through a factory of the same instance. Its user data passes to the registered sink. The caller
still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy), which does not
affect the registered sink.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance to register on.
* `sink`: The log sink to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the log sink on the loading extension's instance, making it available to the logging configuration
under its name.

Use this from the extension's load callback. Registration follows the rules of [`duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink`](#duckdb_v2_instance_register_log_sink).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_log_sink(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle sink,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `sink`: The log sink to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the log sink, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered sink.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_log_sink_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_log_sink_handle *sink
);
```

##### Parameters

* `sink`: The log sink to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Logical Type

#### `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID`

Logical type identifier. The values are the same integers DuckDB uses
internally, so round-tripping is lossless. The bind- and UDF-only ids
(UNKNOWN, ANY, TEMPLATE) appear here for completeness; they do not show
up in result column types in practice.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_INVALID` = 0: Invalid / unset.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_SQLNULL` = 1: NULL constant type.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UNKNOWN` = 2: Unknown — used for unresolved parameter expressions.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_ANY` = 3: ANY — used for functions that accept any type.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TYPE` = 6: A type carried as a value (type parameters). Values of this type are built via value_create_type.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_BOOLEAN` = 10
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TINYINT` = 11
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_SMALLINT` = 12
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_INTEGER` = 13
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_BIGINT` = 14
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_DATE` = 15: 32-bit days since epoch.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIME` = 16: 64-bit microseconds since midnight.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP_SEC` = 17: 64-bit seconds since epoch.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP_MS` = 18: 64-bit milliseconds since epoch.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP` = 19: 64-bit microseconds since epoch.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP_NS` = 20: 64-bit nanoseconds since epoch.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_DECIMAL` = 21: Decimal with width and scale parameters.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_FLOAT` = 22
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_DOUBLE` = 23
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_VARCHAR` = 25
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_BLOB` = 26
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_INTERVAL` = 27
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UTINYINT` = 28
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_USMALLINT` = 29
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UINTEGER` = 30
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UBIGINT` = 31
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP_TZ` = 32: 64-bit microseconds since epoch, timezone-aware.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIMESTAMP_TZ_NS` = 33: 64-bit nanoseconds since epoch, timezone-aware.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIME_TZ` = 34: 64-bit microseconds since midnight + 32-bit offset.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TIME_NS` = 35: 64-bit nanoseconds since midnight.
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_BIT` = 36
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_BIGNUM` = 39: Arbitrary-precision integer (VARINT-encoded).
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UHUGEINT` = 49
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_HUGEINT` = 50
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UUID` = 54
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_GEOMETRY` = 60: Geometry (spatial extension).
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_STRUCT` = 100
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_LIST` = 101
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_MAP` = 102
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_ENUM` = 104
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_UNION` = 107
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_ARRAY` = 108
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_VARIANT` = 109
* `DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID_TUPLE` = 110: Unnamed struct; shares the physical representation of STRUCT.

<br>

<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_factory_create_common_type"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_factory_create_common_type</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">types</span>, <span class="kt">idx_t</span> <span class="nv">type_count</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle</span> *<span class="nv">out_type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a logical type from a type id plus value parameters.

The id-keyed twin of factory_create_type_from_name: the type id names the
kind, and the parameters bind it. With param_count 0 it instantiates a
primitive directly, without touching the catalog: BOOLEAN,
TINYINT..BIGINT, UTINYINT..UBIGINT, HUGEINT, UHUGEINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE,
DATE, every TIME and TIMESTAMP variant, INTERVAL, VARCHAR, BLOB, BIT,
BIGNUM, and UUID. ANY is accepted as well.

ANY is a function-signature wildcard, constructible here so it can be
passed to the function parameter and varargs setters, as a fixed-arity
ANY parameter or an ANY varargs type. Data-creating surfaces reject it:
value and data chunk creation, scalar and aggregate return types, table
function result columns, cast source and target types, and custom type
registration.

With parameters, the id resolves to its canonical built-in type and binds
through the same constructors as factory_create_type_from_name, so the parameterized
kinds construct here too: decimal(width, scale); list(T); array(T, size);
map(K, V); struct(fields); union(members); enum(entries); and varchar
with a named “collation” parameter. Parameters are (name, value) pairs in
two parallel arrays, exactly as for factory_create_type_from_name.

Returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID when param_count is 0 and the id needs
parameters (DECIMAL, LIST, STRUCT, TUPLE, MAP, ARRAY, UNION, ENUM,
VARIANT, GEOMETRY), for the bind-time-only ids (SQLNULL, UNKNOWN), for
TYPE — construct that via factory_create_type_from_text — and for INVALID.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_id(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID type_id,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *param_names,
  const duckdb_v2_value_handle *param_values,
  idx_t param_count,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to resolve the type in.
* `type_id`: The type id to instantiate.
* `param_names`: Optional. An array of param_count parameter names; a {NULL, 0} entry is positional. Pass NULL for all-positional parameters.
* `param_values`: An array of param_count parameter values. Borrowed (copied in). Pass NULL when param_count is 0.
* `param_count`: The number of parameters. 0 instantiates a parameterless primitive.
* `out_type`: Receives the new logical type handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a logical type from a type name plus value parameters.

The generic constructor: resolves the name in the factory's catalog and
binds it with the given parameters, exactly as SQL binds a type
expression. Built-in parameterized kinds and registered extension types
construct through this same call.

An unqualified name is resolved along the search path first and then in
the system catalog, which is where the built-in kinds live. A qualified
name is resolved exactly as written, with no system-catalog fallback, so
it names the type in that catalog or schema or fails.

Parameters are (name, value) pairs in two parallel arrays. param_names
may be NULL to make every parameter positional, and a {NULL, 0} entry
makes that one parameter positional. Child types cross as TYPE values,
built with value_create_type. The
built-in shapes are: decimal(width, scale); list(T); array(T, size);
map(K, V); struct(fields, as named or all-positional TYPE values);
union(members, as named TYPE values); enum(entries, as VARCHAR values);
and varchar with a named “collation” VARCHAR parameter.

A name that resolves to a type with no bind function takes no parameters,
and passing any fails. Bind errors — unknown name, wrong parameter count
or types — surface from the call.

Resolves in the scope of the factory: a connection's or callback's
factory reaches the catalog, an instance's factory knows only the
built-in types. A connection's factory looks up catalog types in the
connection's transaction, or in one of its own when none is open. Through an
instance's factory, only an unqualified built-in name resolves.

The returned logical type is caller-owned and must be destroyed via
logical_type_destroy. A type resolved from the catalog shares
database-owned storage, such as an ENUM dictionary, so destroy it before
closing the database. This is the inverse of
logical_type_get_param_count / logical_type_get_param.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_name(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *param_names,
  const duckdb_v2_value_handle *param_values,
  idx_t param_count,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to resolve the type in.
* `name`: The type name to resolve. Parts are matched case-insensitively; qualify it to name a type in a particular catalog or schema.
* `param_names`: Optional. An array of param_count parameter names; a {NULL, 0} entry is positional. Pass NULL for all-positional parameters.
* `param_values`: An array of param_count parameter values. Borrowed (copied in). Pass NULL when param_count is 0.
* `param_count`: The number of parameters.
* `out_type`: Receives the new logical type handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a logical type by parsing SQL text.

Parses a SQL type expression and returns the bound
logical type. It accepts primitives (“INTEGER”), parameterized kinds
(“DECIMAL(18,3)”, “INTEGER[]”, “STRUCT(a INTEGER, b VARCHAR)”,
“MAP(VARCHAR, INTEGER)”, “INTEGER[3]”, “UNION(i INTEGER, s VARCHAR)”,
“ENUM('a', 'b')”), and catalog-registered type names, both user-defined
and from extensions. A catalog type name binds to its structural type,
and the name is not preserved as an alias. Names are case-insensitive.
Parse and bind errors surface from the call.

Resolves in the scope of the factory: a connection's or callback's
factory reaches the catalog, an instance's factory knows only the
built-in types. A connection's factory looks up catalog types in the
connection's transaction, or in one of its own when none is open. Text naming
only built-in types never touches the catalog.

The returned logical type is caller-owned and must be destroyed via
logical_type_destroy. A type resolved from the catalog shares
database-owned storage, such as an ENUM dictionary, so destroy it before
closing the database. This is the inverse of logical_type_to_text for
every constructible kind.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_from_text(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  const duckdb_v2_str *text,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to resolve the type in.
* `text`: View of the SQL type expression to parse.
* `out_type`: Receives the new logical type handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

On success, writes the new caller-owned handle into *out_type; destroy it

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_copy(
```

* `out_type`: Receives the new logical type handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a logical type handle.

Null-safe: passing nullptr or a slot already set to nullptr is a
no-op. On success the slot is set to nullptr.

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *type
```

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_is_equal`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Compares two logical types for deep equality.

Two types are equal when they agree in kind and in every parameter,
recursively. DECIMAL(10, 2) equals DECIMAL(10, 2), but not DECIMAL(10, 3)
and not FLOAT; two STRUCTs are equal when they have the same field names
in the same order and equal field types.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_is_equal(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle left,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle right,
  bool *result,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `left`: The first logical type.
* `right`: The second logical type.
* `result`: Receives the result of the comparison. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_id`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the logical type id.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_id(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  DUCKDB_V2_LOGICAL_TYPE_ID *out_id,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The logical type.
* `out_id`: Receives the type id. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the logical type's name.

The alias when one is set — an extension or user-defined name such as
`POINT_2D` — otherwise the canonical name of the type id, such as
“INTEGER”, “DECIMAL”, or “TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE”. Never the empty
view. This is exactly the name vocabulary create_type_from_name accepts.
The view is valid until the logical type is destroyed; a canonical name
points at static storage.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_name(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *out_name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The logical type.
* `out_name`: Receives a borrowed view of the name (alias when set, else the id's canonical name). (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_to_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Renders a logical type as SQL text.

An aliased type renders as its alias, and create_type_from_text resolves
that spelling only when the name is registered in the factory's
catalog. The text round-trips through create_type_from_text for every
constructible kind, with one exception: ANY renders as “ANY”, but
create_type_from_text cannot parse it back, since ANY is a signature
wildcard rather than a parseable SQL type.

Writes into a caller-supplied buffer, so nothing is allocated on the
caller's behalf and nothing has to be freed. Pass out_text = NULL to size
the buffer without rendering into it: out_length then receives the
length, and out_capacity is ignored. With out_text != NULL, out_capacity
must be at least out_length + 1, or the call returns
ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE with out_length set to the required length and
out_text left untouched.

out_length never counts the terminator, but a successful write always
appends one, so the buffer is usable as a C string.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_to_text(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  char *out_text,
  idx_t out_capacity,
  idx_t *out_length,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The logical type.
* `out_text`: Caller-owned buffer receiving the text plus a null terminator, or NULL to only report the required length in out_length. (out)
* `out_capacity`: Bytes available in out_text, terminator included. Ignored when out_text is NULL.
* `out_length`: Receives the text length excluding the null terminator — written on success and on ERROR_INPUT_OBJECT_SIZE. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_param_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of value parameters of a logical type.

The inspection dual of create_type_from_name: these are the parameters
that reconstruct the type through it. Per kind: DECIMAL 2 (width, scale);
LIST 1 (element type); ARRAY 2 (element type, size); MAP 2 (key type,
value type); STRUCT and TUPLE one per field; UNION one per member; ENUM
one per dictionary entry; VARCHAR 1 when a collation is set, else 0;
GEOMETRY 1 when a coordinate system is set, else 0; everything else 0. A
bound type reports only what it actually carries, so a bind-time modifier
that is not retained — an ignored VARCHAR length, say — does not
reappear.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_param_count(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The logical type.
* `out_count`: Receives the number of parameters. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_param`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns one value parameter of a logical type.

out_name receives a borrowed view of the parameter name — a STRUCT field
name, a UNION member name, “collation” — or the empty view {NULL, 0} for
a positional parameter. A non-empty view is valid until the logical type
is destroyed. out_value receives an owned value, destroyed via
value_destroy: child types come back as TYPE values (unwrap them with
value_get_type), DECIMAL width and scale as UTINYINT, ARRAY size as
BIGINT, and ENUM dictionary entries and collations as VARCHAR. An
out-of-range index returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. Each call allocates one
owned value.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_logical_type_get_param(
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle type,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *out_name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle *out_value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `type`: The logical type.
* `index`: The parameter index, in [0, param_count).
* `out_name`: Receives a borrowed view of the parameter name, or the empty view {NULL, 0} for a positional parameter. (out, borrowed)
* `out_value`: Receives the owned parameter value. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_with_alias`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a logical type that is an alias of another logical type.

The alias keeps the base type's internal representation, so executing
against it needs no special handling, while remaining logically distinct
from the base type. Intended for custom type bind callbacks, where both
the base type and the name come from the bind info.

The alias is not registered anywhere, so this works through any
factory. An empty alias name returns
ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_factory_create_type_with_alias(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle base_type,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *alias_name,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to resolve the type in.
* `base_type`: The logical type to alias. Typically the base type supplied in the custom type bind info.
* `alias_name`: The name for the resulting type. Typically the name of the custom type being constructed, also available from the bind info.
* `out_type`: Receives the new type: the base type's internal representation under the given alias name. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_factory_create_common_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates the common type of a set of logical types.

The common type is the type every input implicitly casts to, resolved by
the same rule a SQL list literal and value_create_list follow:
INTEGER and BIGINT resolve to BIGINT, and DECIMAL(4,1) and DECIMAL(5,4)
to DECIMAL(7,4). The types are combined pairwise from left to right, and
the result is not guaranteed to be independent of their order.

A connection's or a callback's factory also applies the casts that
extensions registered, while an instance's factory knows only the
built-in ones, so the two can resolve the same set differently. A single
type resolves to a copy of itself.

Returns ERROR_INPUT_INVALID for an empty set, for a NULL entry and for
ANY, and ERROR_QUERY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED when the types have no common type.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_factory_create_common_type(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  const duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *types,
  idx_t type_count,
  duckdb_v2_logical_type_handle *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to resolve the type in.
* `types`: An array of type_count logical types. Borrowed.
* `type_count`: The number of types. Must be at least 1.
* `out_type`: Receives the new logical type handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Macro

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a macro function being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_create), configured
with [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body) and the signature obtained via
[`duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature), made available with [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function), and destroyed
with [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_MACRO_FUNCTION_TYPE`

The kind of a macro function, deciding how its body is read. Pass one to [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_create).

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_MACRO_FUNCTION_TYPE_SCALAR` = 0: A scalar macro. The body is a single expression, and the macro is called like a scalar function.
* `DUCKDB_V2_MACRO_FUNCTION_TYPE_TABLE` = 1: A table macro. The body is a single SELECT query, and the macro is called like a table function.

<br>

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_create"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_create</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_factory_handle</span> <span class="nv">factory</span>, <span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_MACRO_FUNCTION_TYPE</span> <span class="nv">type</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> *<span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_identifier_t</span> *<span class="nv">name</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">const</span> <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_str</span> *<span class="nv">body</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle</span> *<span class="nv">sig</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle</span> *<span class="nv">docs</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_extension_handle</span> <span class="nv">extension</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> <span class="nv">function</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);
<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle</span> *<span class="nv">function</span>);
</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new macro function through a factory.

The macro function starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions and the signature obtained via
[`duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature), then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function). The
caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy), also after registration.

The macro function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  DUCKDB_V2_MACRO_FUNCTION_TYPE type,
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the macro function through.
* `type`: Whether the macro is a scalar or a table macro.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created macro function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the macro function, as SQL calls it.

The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name. A name must be set before
registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The macro function to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the body of the macro function, as SQL text.

For a scalar macro the body is a single expression, for a table macro a single SELECT query. It refers to the
parameters by name. The body is parsed at registration, which fails on a syntax error; names in it are resolved
only when the macro is called, as with SQL `CREATE MACRO`. The body is borrowed and copied. Calling this again
replaces the previous body. A body must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_set_body(
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_str *body,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The macro function to set the body of.
* `body`: The SQL text of the body. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the macro function's signature so its parameters can be declared.

Add parameters with [`duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter`](#duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter). A macro's parameters can always be passed by
position or by name, so only `FUNCTION_PARAMETER_KIND_STANDARD` parameters are accepted; a macro has no variadic
parameters. A parameter of type ANY is untyped, and a parameter with a default value can be omitted by a caller.
A macro's result is decided by its body, so the signature cannot set a return type. Registration fails on a
signature that does not follow these rules. The signature is modified in place.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature(
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle *sig,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The macro function to get the signature of.
* `sig`: The returned signature. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the macro function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the documentation of the macro function so it can be filled in.

Set a description with [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description), and add examples and categories with
[`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example) and [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category). The documentation is modified in place and
registered with the macro function. Optional.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_docs(
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle *docs,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The macro function to get the documentation of.
* `docs`: The returned documentation. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the macro function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the macro function, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The macro function is registered on the loading extension's database and attributed to the extension. Use this
from the extension's load callback. Registration requires a name and a body that parses, and a signature that
follows the rules of [`duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_get_signature). It fails when a function of the same name already
exists: a macro function has a single overload. The macro function must have been created through a factory of
the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered macro function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_macro_function(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `function`: The macro function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the macro function, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered
macro function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_macro_function_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_macro_function_handle *function
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The macro function to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Pragma

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom pragma function being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_create),
configured with the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback),
etc.) and the signature obtained via [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature), made available with
[`duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function), and destroyed with
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the result of a pragma function's “query” callback. The query callback receives this
handle next to a [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle), which gives access to the arguments and the user data, and uses it to
set the query to run in place of the `PRAGMA` statement.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_info_handle result,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the arguments of the `PRAGMA` statement and the user data.
* `result`: Borrowed opaque handle to set the query to run in place of the `PRAGMA` statement through.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_exec_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_pragma_function_exec_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the arguments of the `PRAGMA` statement and the user data.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>
