#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new pragma function through a factory.

The function starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name),
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback), etc.) and the signature obtained via [`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature),
then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function) or
[`duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function). The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy), also after registration.

The pragma function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the pragma function through.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created pragma function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the pragma function, as the `PRAGMA` statement calls it.

The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name.
A name must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_docs`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the documentation of the function so it can be filled in.

Set a description with [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_set_description), and add examples and categories with
[`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_example) and [`duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category`](#duckdb_v2_function_docs_add_category). The documentation is modified in place and
registered with the function. Optional.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_docs(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_docs_handle *docs,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to get the documentation of.
* `docs`: The returned documentation. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the function's signature so it can be configured.

Add parameters with [`duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter`](#duckdb_v2_function_signature_add_parameter). A pragma produces no value, so its signature cannot
set a return type. A signature without parameters makes a pragma called as `PRAGMA name`. The signature is
modified in place.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_get_signature(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_function_signature_handle *sig,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to get the signature of.
* `sig`: The returned signature. Borrowed and valid for the lifetime of the function handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the pragma function.

Associates an opaque pointer with the function, retrievable from the callbacks via
[`duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_user_data). The opaque handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor, invoked
when the data is no longer needed.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the query callback of the pragma function, making it a query pragma.

The query callback is invoked before the `PRAGMA` statement is bound, and must set a SQL string through
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_set_query`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_set_query). The string is parsed and its statements run in place of the `PRAGMA`
statement. A pragma function has either a query callback or an exec callback; registration fails when both or
neither are set.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_query_callback(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the query callback of.
* `callback`: The query callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_exec_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the exec callback of the pragma function, making it an exec pragma.

The exec callback is invoked when the `PRAGMA` statement executes, and runs for its side effects: the statement
produces no rows. A pragma function has either a query callback or an exec callback; registration fails when
both or neither are set.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_set_exec_callback(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_exec_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the exec callback of.
* `callback`: The exec callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_set_query`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the SQL to run in place of the `PRAGMA` statement.

The query may hold several statements, separated by semicolons. It is borrowed and copied. Calling this again
replaces the previous query. The query callback must set a query.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_set_query(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_query_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_str *query,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The query info handle.
* `query`: The SQL to run. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the pragma function, making it available to the `PRAGMA` statement.

The function is registered on the connection's database, visible to every connection, in the connection's
transaction: inside an explicit transaction, it is invisible to other connections until the transaction commits,
and a rollback undoes it. Registration requires a name and exactly one of a query callback or an exec callback,
and fails when a pragma of the same name already exists. The pragma function must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_pragma_function(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `function`: The pragma function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the pragma function, making it available to the `PRAGMA` statement.

The function is registered on the loading extension's database and attributed to the extension. Use this from the
extension's load callback. Registration requires a name and exactly one of a query callback or an exec callback,
and fails when a pragma of the same name already exists. The pragma function must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy), which does not affect the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_pragma_function(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `function`: The pragma function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the pragma function, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered
function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_pragma_function_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_pragma_function_handle *function
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Replacement Scan

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a replacement scan being built. Created with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_create`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_create),
configured with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback) and [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data), made available
with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan), [`duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan), and destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a replacement scan when the binder consults it. The
callback receives this handle and can use it to inspect the unresolved name and to claim it by naming what to
read instead. Valid only for the duration of the callback; the name it hands out is owned separately and
outlives it.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

<span class="kt">DUCKDB_V2_ERROR</span> <a href="#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback"><span class="nf">duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback</span></a>(<span class="kt">duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle</span> <span class="nv">scan</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_callback_fn</span> <span class="nv">callback</span>, <span class="kt">duckdb_v2_error_info_handle</span> *<span class="nv">err</span>);

</code></pre></div></div>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new replacement scan through a factory.

The scan starts out empty: configure it with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback) and optionally
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data), then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan), [`duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan). The caller owns the
returned handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy), also after registration.

The scan can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle *scan,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the scan through.
* `scan`: On success, receives the newly created replacement scan. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the callback of the replacement scan.

The callback is invoked during query planning for each table reference the catalog could not resolve. It can
inspect the unresolved name via [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_name), and claim the
reference via [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name), [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection) or
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery); returning without claiming declines it. The context passed to the callback
may be used to read settings, but not to run queries. A callback must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_callback(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle scan,
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_callback_fn callback,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `scan`: The scan to set the callback of.
* `callback`: The callback to set.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets arbitrary user data on the replacement scan.

Associates an opaque pointer with the scan, retrievable from the callback via
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_user_data). The opaque handle bundles the pointer with an optional destructor,
invoked when the data is no longer needed, at the latest when the scan's scope ends. The callback may be
invoked from several connections at once, so the data must be safe to read concurrently.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle scan,
  duckdb_v2_opaque *data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `scan`: The scan to set the user data of.
* `data`: Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_user_data`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the user data set via [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_user_data).

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_user_data(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  void **data,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `data`: Receives the user data pointer, or null if none was set. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Retrieves the name the catalog could not resolve.

The name as written in the query, as a path: an unqualified reference has a single part, and a qualified one
carries its catalog and schema before it -- see [`duckdb_v2_qname_get_part`](#duckdb_v2_qname_get_part). For a file-backed reference the single
part is the path with the quotes stripped. The returned name is owned by the caller and must be destroyed via
[`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy); being owned, it may outlive the callback.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_get_name(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `name`: Receives the unresolved name. Owned by the caller; destroy via [`duckdb_v2_qname_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_qname_destroy). (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Claims the reference by naming a table function to read instead.

Arguments to the function are added with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_argument`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_argument) and
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_named_argument`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_named_argument). The name is borrowed and copied, and its parts are matched
case-insensitively. A qualified name targets a function in a particular schema or catalog, exactly as writing
it out in SQL would. The name is not resolved here: an unknown function fails later, when the replacement is
bound. Calling this again replaces the previous name and keeps the arguments added so far.

The three claim forms, [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name), [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection) and
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery), are mutually exclusive: claiming the reference through a second, different
form results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_qname_handle name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `name`: The table function to read instead. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_argument`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Appends a positional argument to the claimed table function.

Positional arguments are passed in the order they are added, before any named ones. The value is borrowed and
copied, so the caller may destroy it after the call. Requires [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name) to have
been called first; otherwise the call results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_argument(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `value`: The argument value. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_named_argument`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Appends a named argument to the claimed table function.

Equivalent to writing `name := value` at the call site. The name and the value are borrowed and copied, so the
caller may destroy the value after the call. Requires [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name) to have been
called first; otherwise the call results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_add_named_argument(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_value_handle value,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `name`: The name of the parameter to bind the value to. Borrowed and copied.
* `value`: The argument value. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Claims the reference by naming a column data collection to read instead.

The collection is borrowed, not copied: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive, and must not clear,
reset or destroy it, for as long as any result reading it is live, since the result scans its buffers directly.

A prepared statement extends that lifetime well beyond its own results. Preparing a statement over a claimed
name captures the borrow in the plan, and since a collection claim reads no database there is nothing to
invalidate that plan: [`duckdb_v2_prepared_statement_reuses_plan`](#duckdb_v2_prepared_statement_reuses_plan) reports true, and every later execution reuses the
captured borrow without consulting the callback again. So dropping the name from whatever the callback resolves
against does not release the collection, and releasing it while such a statement is live leaves the next
execution reading freed memory. Destroy every prepared statement over a claimed name before clearing,
resetting or destroying the collection behind it.

By default the collection's columns are named col1..colN. Pass `column_names` to name them instead. When
supplied, `column_count` must equal the collection's column count and no name may be empty; pass NULL and 0
for the default names.

The three claim forms, [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name), [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection) and
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery), are mutually exclusive: claiming the reference through a second, different
form results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *column_names,
  idx_t column_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `collection`: The collection to read instead. Borrowed; the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive.
* `column_names`: Optional. An array of `column_count` column names, in order. Pass NULL for the default names col1..colN.
* `column_count`: The number of names in `column_names`. Must equal the collection's column count, or 0 for the default names.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Claims the reference by naming a query to read instead.

The text is parsed at the call and must contain exactly one SELECT statement: a syntax error, several
statements or a statement of another kind results in an error. The text is borrowed for the call only. Prefer
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name) when a single table function call suffices, as it avoids the parse
and keeps the plan flatter.

The three claim forms, [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_function_name), [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_collection) and
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery), are mutually exclusive: claiming the reference through a second, different
form results in an error.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_subquery(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_str *sql,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `sql`: The SELECT statement to read instead. Borrowed for the call only.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_alias`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the alias the claimed replacement is bound under.

Optional, and independent of the claim form. An alias written in the query takes precedence over this one;
without either, the table name of the reference is used, which for a file-backed reference is the path. The
alias is borrowed and copied.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_set_alias(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_info_handle info,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *alias,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The info handle.
* `alias`: The alias to bind the replacement under. Borrowed and copied.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the replacement scan, making it consulted for names the catalog cannot resolve.

The scan is visible only to queries on this connection and is released when the connection is destroyed. It is
consulted before every instance-wide scan, so it can claim a name that a built-in scan would otherwise take.
Registration requires a callback. Scans are consulted in registration order within their scope, connection-scoped
ones before instance-wide ones, and the first to claim a name wins. A scan cannot be registered twice, and a
registered scan cannot be unregistered: it lives until its scope ends. The scan must have been created through a
factory of the same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy), which does not affect the registered scan.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_replacement_scan(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle scan,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `scan`: The replacement scan to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the replacement scan, making it consulted for names the catalog cannot resolve.

The scan is visible to every connection to the instance and lives until the instance is destroyed. Registering it
while queries are binding on other connections is not thread-safe: register before issuing queries. Registration
requires a callback. Scans are consulted in registration order within their scope, connection-scoped ones before
instance-wide ones, and the first to claim a name wins. A scan cannot be registered twice, and a registered scan
cannot be unregistered: it lives until its scope ends. The scan must have been created through a factory of the
same database. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with
[`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy), which does not affect the registered scan.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_instance_register_replacement_scan(
  duckdb_v2_instance_handle instance,
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle scan,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `instance`: The instance to register on.
* `scan`: The replacement scan to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the replacement scan, making it consulted for names the catalog cannot resolve.

The scan is visible to every connection to the loading extension's instance and lives until the instance is
destroyed. Use this from the extension's load callback. Registration requires a callback. Scans are consulted in
registration order within their scope, connection-scoped ones before instance-wide ones, and the first to claim a
name wins. A scan cannot be registered twice, and a registered scan cannot be unregistered: it lives until its
scope ends. The scan must have been created through a factory of the same database. The caller still owns the
handle after registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy), which does not affect the
registered scan.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_replacement_scan(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle scan,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `scan`: The replacement scan to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the replacement scan, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered scan.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_replacement_scan_handle *scan
);
```

##### Parameters

* `scan`: The scan to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### Scalar

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle`

An owned opaque handle to a custom scalar function being built. Created with
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_create`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_create), configured with the
setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name), [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_exec_callback`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_exec_callback), etc.) and the
signature obtained via [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_signature), made available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function), and
destroyed with [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy).

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the result of a scalar function's “resolve types” phase. The “resolve types”
callback receives this handle next to a [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle), which gives access to the arguments and the
user data, and can use it to set the return type of the call site being bound.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the result of a scalar function's “bind” phase. The “bind” callback receives this
handle next to a [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle), which gives access to the arguments and the user data, and can use
it to set the bind data of the call site being bound.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_init_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a scalar function during the local state initialization 
“init” phase. The “init” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. set up local state reusable across 
invocations of the “exec” execution callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_info_handle`

A borrowed opaque handle to the arguments supplied to a scalar function during the execution “exec” phase. 
The “exec” callback receives this handle and can use it to e.g. access the input argument vectors, 
retrieve the number of rows to process, and write results to the output vector.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_info_handle result,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the arguments of the call site being bound and the user data.
* `result`: Borrowed opaque handle to set the return type of the call site being bound through.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_info_handle result,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the arguments of the call site being bound and the user data.
* `result`: Borrowed opaque handle to set the bind data of the call site being bound through.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_init_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_scalar_function_init_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_init_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_callback_fn`

##### Syntax

```c
typedef void (*duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_callback_fn)(
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_info_handle info,
  duckdb_v2_context_handle context,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: Borrowed opaque handle providing access to the information available to the callback.
* `context`: Borrowed handle to the context of the query currently executing the callback.
* `err`: Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_create`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Creates a new scalar function through a factory.

The function starts out empty: configure it with the setter functions (e.g. [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name),
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_exec_callback`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_exec_callback), etc.) and the signature obtained via [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_signature`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_get_signature),
then make it available with [`duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function`](#duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function) or [`duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function`](#duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function).
The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy), also after
registration.

The scalar function can only be registered on the database the factory belongs to.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_scalar_function_create(
  duckdb_v2_factory_handle factory,
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle *function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `factory`: The factory to create the scalar function through.
* `function`: On success, receives the newly created scalar function. Owned by the caller. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the name of the scalar function.

The name is borrowed and copied. Calling this again replaces the previous name.
A name must be set before registration.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_name(
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle function,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to set the name of.
* `name`: The name to set. Borrowed and copied.

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_resolve_types_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional resolve types callback of the scalar function.

The resolve types callback is invoked during query planning for each call site of the function, before the
arguments are cast to the parameter types of the signature. Through its [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle) it can
inspect the argument types as they were passed and constant argument values. Through its
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_resolve_types_info_handle) it can set a concrete return type. It cannot set “bind data”, use the
bind callback for that.

##### Syntax


`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_set_bind_callback`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Sets the optional bind callback of the scalar function.

The bind callback is invoked during query planning for each call site of the function, after the resolve
types callback and after the arguments have been cast to the parameter types of the signature. Through its
[`duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_info_handle) it can inspect the argument types and constant argument values. Through its
[`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_info_handle`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_bind_info_handle) it can set “bind data” that is shared with the init and exec callbacks. It
cannot change the types of the call site, use the resolve types callback for that.

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns how many rows this execution must produce. The exec callback
must write exactly this many rows to the result vector. Note that this
may be less than a full vector: with all-constant arguments the function


##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_get_arg_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns how many argument vectors this invocation carries, split into the four parts of the argument list.

The parts and their order are those the bind callback saw through [`duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count`](#duckdb_v2_function_bind_get_arg_count), and the
vectors are at the same indices. Valid indices for [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_get_arg`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_get_arg) are [0, the sum of the four
counts). Every out-parameter may be NULL, in which case nothing is written to it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_get_arg_count(
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_exec_info_handle info,
  idx_t *positional_fixed,
  idx_t *positional_variadic,
  idx_t *named_fixed,
  idx_t *named_variadic,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `info`: The exec info handle.
* `positional_fixed`: Optional. Receives the number of positional-only and standard parameters. (out)
* `positional_variadic`: Optional. Receives the number of arguments `*args` received, 0 when the signature has none. (out)
* `named_fixed`: Optional. Receives the number of named-only parameters. (out)
* `named_variadic`: Optional. Receives the number of arguments `**kwargs` received, 0 when the signature has none. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the scalar function, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The function is registered on the connection's database, visible to every connection, in the connection's
transaction: inside an explicit transaction, it is invisible to other connections until the transaction commits,
and a rollback undoes it. Registration requires a name, an exec callback, and a signature with a complete return
type; an ANY return type is accepted only together with a resolve types callback that sets the concrete type per
call site. The scalar function must have been created through a factory of the same database. The caller still
owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy), which does not affect
the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_connection_register_scalar_function(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection to register on.
* `function`: The scalar function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Registers the scalar function, making it available for use in SQL queries.

The function is registered on the loading extension's database and attributed to the extension. Use this from the
extension's load callback. Registration requires a name, an exec callback, and a signature with a complete return
type; an ANY return type is accepted only together with a resolve types callback that sets the concrete type per
call site. The scalar function must have been created through a factory of the same database. The caller still
owns the handle after registration and must destroy it with [`duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy), which does not affect
the registered function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_extension_register_scalar_function(
  duckdb_v2_extension_handle extension,
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle function,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `extension`: The loading extension.
* `function`: The scalar function to register.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy).

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys the scalar function, releasing its resources.

Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to
prevent double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered
function.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_scalar_function_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_scalar_function_handle *function
);
```

##### Parameters

* `function`: The function to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

### SQL Statement

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to a single parsed SQL statement, produced by
statement_iterator_next. statement_execute runs it without consuming it;
the caller always destroys it via sql_statement_destroy.

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_handle`

An opaque, owned handle to an iterator over the statements of a SQL
string, produced by parse_sql. Destroy it via statement_iterator_destroy;
statements it already yielded are independently owned and unaffected.

<br>

#### `DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE`

SQL statement type of a parsed statement or an executed query.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE_INVALID` = 0
* `DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE_SELECT` = 1
* `DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE_INSERT` = 2
* `DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE_UPDATE` = 3

#### `duckdb_v2_parse_sql`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Parses a SQL string into an iterator over its statements.

Parses and nothing more: no binding, no catalog access, no transaction.
The connection supplies the parser options and parser extensions, and is
not otherwise touched. Statements are raw parser output; statement-level
rewrites happen inside statement_execute. The SQL string is copied, so
the caller may free it once this call returns. An input with no
statements — empty, whitespace, or separators only — yields an iterator
that is immediately exhausted.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_parse_sql(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  const char *sql,
  duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_handle *out_iterator,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection supplying the parser configuration.
* `sql`: Null-terminated SQL string; may contain any number of statements.
* `out_iterator`: Receives the new iterator handle. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_next`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Yields the next statement, or NULL when exhausted.

On success *out_statement receives the next owned statement, or NULL once
the iterator is exhausted — repeatedly, so calling again is harmless. A
parse error within the input surfaces no later than the call that reaches
the failing statement: an implementation that parses eagerly reports it
from parse_sql instead and yields no statements at all, while an
incremental one yields the statements ahead of the failure first. On
failure *out_statement is set to NULL.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_next(
  duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_handle iterator,
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle *out_statement,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `iterator`: The iterator to advance.
* `out_statement`: Receives an owned statement, or NULL when the iterator is exhausted. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_statement_bind`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Binds a parsed statement without executing, yielding its schema signature.

Preprocesses and binds the statement exactly as execution would, but runs
nothing: the result is the statement's signature as two schemas, not a
query result. The statement is borrowed, not consumed, so it can be bound
as often as you like and executed later. out_schema receives the output
schema (result columns) and is never empty, since a non-SELECT reports a
single status column: a BIGINT changed-rows count, or a BOOLEAN success.
out_parameters, when non-NULL, receives the input schema (parameter
types, ordered by binding index). Both are owned; destroy them via
schema_destroy.

Binding is read-only and does not disturb a live result: it begins no
query, claims no cursor, reuses an active transaction read-only, and runs
alongside a paused stream. It is single-consumer like the stepping
functions, so bind concurrently only on a second connection.
Prepare-time errors — binder, catalog, preprocessing — surface here. A
statement that expands into a group (a dynamic PIVOT, or
statement-expanding DDL such as ALTER ADD COLUMN with a non-constant
DEFAULT) has a schema known only at execution, and is reported with
ERROR_INPUT_METADATA_DEFERRED; execute it instead.

*out_schema and *out_parameters are set to NULL on failure.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_statement_bind(
  duckdb_v2_connection_handle conn,
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  duckdb_v2_schema_handle *out_schema,
  duckdb_v2_schema_handle *out_parameters,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `conn`: The connection supplying the catalog, transaction, and parser configuration.
* `statement`: The statement to bind. Borrowed; not consumed.
* `out_schema`: Receives the owned output schema (result columns). Destroy via schema_destroy. (out)
* `out_parameters`: Optional. When non-NULL, receives the owned input schema (parameter types, ordered by binding index). Destroy via schema_destroy. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_statement_add_collection`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Binds a column data collection to the statement under a name.

Makes the collection visible to the statement as a table named `name`, by adding a common table expression to
the parsed statement. The statement can then be bound, prepared or executed as usual; each execution reads the
collection's contents at that moment, so a prepared statement can be executed again after the collection was
cleared and refilled. Supported statement types are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE INTO; any other
type is rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`.

A name the statement already defines as a common table expression, in its SQL text or by a prior call, is
rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. The binding shadows any catalog table named `name`, as a common table
expression does.

By default the collection's columns are named col1..colN. Pass `column_names` to name them instead; when
supplied, `column_count` must equal the collection's column count. Pass NULL and 0 for the default names.

The collection is borrowed: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive, and must not clear, reset or
destroy it, for as long as the statement, any statement copied or prepared from it, or any result executing it
is live. An empty collection is a valid binding. Several collections can be bound under distinct names.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_statement_add_collection(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *name,
  duckdb_v2_column_data_collection_handle collection,
  const duckdb_v2_identifier_t *column_names,
  idx_t column_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement to bind the collection to. Modified in place.
* `name`: The non-empty name the statement refers to the collection by. Borrowed and copied.
* `collection`: The collection to bind. Borrowed; the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive.
* `column_names`: Optional. An array of `column_count` names for the collection's columns, in order. Pass NULL for col1..colN.
* `column_count`: The number of names in `column_names`. 0 for the default names; otherwise the collection's column count.
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via [`duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy`](#duckdb_v2_error_info_destroy). (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_type`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the statement's type as classified by the parser.

This gives the type before the statement-level rewrites that
[`duckdb_v2_statement_execute`](#duckdb_v2_statement_execute) applies, if any. So a PRAGMA reports PRAGMA even
where execution rewrites it into a SELECT or a CALL.
[`duckdb_v2_result_get_statement_type`](#duckdb_v2_result_get_statement_type) on the executed result reports the
rewritten type of a statement that rewrites into one. A statement the
parser expands into a group reports MULTI, here and on its result. Its
parts are not visible here, and statement_bind reports
ERROR_INPUT_METADATA_DEFERRED for it.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_type(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  DUCKDB_V2_STATEMENT_TYPE *out_type,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement.
* `out_type`: Receives the statement type. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_text`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the statement's own SQL text.

The slice of the parsed string that belongs to this statement. A
trailing terminator and the whitespace after it are included, whitespace
and comments before the first token are not. The statement holds its own
copy, so the view outlives the SQL string passed to parse_sql and the
iterator, and stays valid until the statement is destroyed. A statement
produced by a parser extension that overrides parsing carries whatever
text the extension recorded.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_text(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  duckdb_v2_str *out_text,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement.
* `out_text`: Receives a borrowed view of the statement text, valid until the statement is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_parameter_count`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Returns the number of distinct parameters the statement declares.

This counts the parameters the parser found ($1, ?, $name, ...), so it
needs no catalog and no binding; only the parameter types wait for
[`duckdb_v2_statement_bind`](#duckdb_v2_statement_bind). Repeated uses of one parameter count once.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_parameter_count(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  idx_t *out_count,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement.
* `out_count`: Receives the number of distinct parameters. (out)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_parameter_name`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Borrows the name of one parameter, in binding order.

Parse-time metadata. Positions follow the parameters' binding indices,
the order of [`duckdb_v2_statement_bind`](#duckdb_v2_statement_bind)'s parameter schema, so position i here
names field i there. The name is the binding key that
[`duckdb_v2_statement_execute`](#duckdb_v2_statement_execute) accepts: “1”, “2”, ... for a positional parameter
($1 or ?), the identifier for a named one ($name). Positional indices may
be gapped ($1 and $3 without $2), in which case the names are “1” and “3”
at positions 0 and 1. The view is valid until the statement is destroyed.
An index outside [0, count) is rejected with ERROR_INPUT_OUT_OF_RANGE.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_sql_statement_get_parameter_name(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle statement,
  idx_t index,
  duckdb_v2_identifier_t *out_name,
  duckdb_v2_error_info_handle *err
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement.
* `index`: Zero-based position in binding order.
* `out_name`: Receives a borrowed view of the parameter name, valid until the statement is destroyed. (out, borrowed)
* `err`: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via error_info_destroy. (out)

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_sql_statement_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a statement handle.

Null-safe: passing nullptr or a slot already set to nullptr is a no-op.
statement_execute does not consume a statement, so every statement is
destroyed here once it is no longer needed. On success the slot is set to
nullptr.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_sql_statement_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_sql_statement_handle *statement
);
```

##### Parameters

* `statement`: The statement to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

<br>

#### `duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_destroy`

Unstable since 2.0.0.

Destroys a statement iterator handle.

Null-safe: passing nullptr or a slot already set to nullptr is a no-op.
Statements already yielded are independently owned and stay valid. On
success the slot is set to nullptr.

##### Syntax

```c
DUCKDB_V2_ERROR duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_destroy(
  duckdb_v2_statement_iterator_handle *iterator
);
```

##### Parameters

* `iterator`: The iterator to destroy.

##### Return Value

`DUCKDB_V2_ERROR`

#### `DUCKDB_V2_VECTOR_TYPE`

Internal representation of a vector, with FSST / SEQUENCE / SHREDDED
collapsed into OTHER: the view getter rejects those and requires an
explicit vector_flatten first. OTHER is the 0-value, so a
zero-initialized out-param reads as “unspecified, needs flatten” rather
than silently looking like FLAT.

##### Values

* `DUCKDB_V2_VECTOR_TYPE_OTHER` = 0: Default for zero-init. Covers FSST / SEQUENCE / SHREDDED — call vector_flatten first.
* `DUCKDB_V2_VECTOR_TYPE_FLAT` = 1: Standard per-row storage.
* `DUCKDB_V2_VECTOR_TYPE_CONSTANT` = 2: A single value applies to every row in the vector.
* `DUCKDB_V2_VECTOR_TYPE_DICTIONARY` = 3: Data + selection vector indirection into another vector.

<br>
